rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish the federal facility and provide all services inclusive of a trained and qualified management staff, supervision, manpower, relief officers, uniforms, equipment, vehicles, and supplies (which includes firearms, ammunition, body restraints, non-lethal devices, body armor, radios, and cellular telephones) to provide support seven (7) days per week, twenty-four (24) hours per day.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish facility, staff, equipment and supplies to provide services 24/7.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide safe and secure conditions of confinement based on the individual characteristics of a diverse population, including threat to the community, risk of flight, type and status of immigration proceeding, community ties, medical and behavioral health issues.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide safe/secure confinement conditions based on detainee risk characteristics.

rows.verbatim: The federal detention facility shall provide easy access to legal services; abundant natural light throughout the federal detention facility; ample indoor and outdoor recreation shall be offered at a reasonable time of day.
rows.normalized: Facility shall provide legal access, natural light, and recreation at reasonable times.

rows.verbatim: Weather permitting, each detainee shall have access for at least one hour per day, five days per week, that allows for vigorous aerobic exercise with extended hours of availability.
rows.normalized: Facility must provide detainees at least 1 hour/day, 5 days/week of vigorous exercise access, weather permitting.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall also provide private showers and restrooms (where practicable); cafeteria style meal service or satellite feeding; institutional alien clothing; contact and non-contact visitation in accordance with NDS 2026; private areas for attorney-client visits, with video teleconferencing capabilities; noise control; enhanced, but controlled freedom of movement (although the manner and degree of implementation may vary based on security levels); enhanced law library and legal resources (including computers with limited web access to accommodate the ICE provided online law library via the ICE Portal); and enhanced programming, including religious services and social programs and dedicated space for religious services.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide showers, meals, clothing, visitation, law library, and programming services as listed.

rows.verbatim: In addition to comprehensive detention services, the Contractor shall provide comprehensive operations and maintenance (O&M) services including ongoing preventive and corrective maintenance, facility operations, post-closing services, and compliance with safety, environmental, medical, IT/communications, accessibility, pest control, and security requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide comprehensive O&M services including maintenance, operations, and compliance areas listed.

ICE detention standards listed in the Addendum – Facility-Specific Requirements.

All furniture shall be furnished by the Contractor in

rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish all EOIR furniture per ICE/EOIR design standards.

EOIR Support Space must be provided per the ICE/EOIR

A separate, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant, entrance for judges and staff is required with

The Contractor shall implement all general housekeeping, environmental cleaning, and disinfection

The Contractor shall comply with all applicable ICE
standards and policies, federal laws, statutes, regulations, and codes.

disturbance control teams consisting of at least 12 people on each team.

transportation to key sites shall be provided as necessary and additional transportation requirements

Duties performed by these officers shall not incur any additional expenses to the
Government.

rows.normalized: A single staff member may transport a single alien only in emergencies and only when same sex as the alien.

is an expectation that a pat search will occur during transport, an assigned transportation staff
member of the same sex as the detainee(s) must be present to conduct the pat search.
rows.normalized: If a pat search is expected during transport, a same-sex staff member must be present to conduct it.

rows.verbatim:
Vehicles and transportation officers must
meet applicable state and federal DOT and firearm laws.
rows.normalized: Vehicles and transportation officers must meet applicable state/federal DOT and firearm laws.

The contractor shall
ensure the material is kept confidential and not viewed by any person other than the authorized

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide fully operational radios to each contract staff (including relief staff).

contractor shall transport the detainee back to the detention facility upon release.

requirements will include facility transfers and movement of detainees to the flight line.

transportation vehicles.

contractor is not restricted from acquiring additional vehicles as deemed necessary; however,

contractor shall not allow employees to use their privately-owned vehicles to transport aliens.

rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain advance approval from the COR or ICE Designated Service Official before incurring overnight lodging from transportation services.

rows.normalized: Contractor must submit a monthly report to TRPAS including at minimum the required trip information per G-391 and a copy of the COR monthly report.

rows.normalized: Contractor must email the G-391 Excel Upload Template and accompanying report to TRPAS, with a copy to the COR, monthly within 5 business days of COR invoice acceptance.

rows.verbatim:
If ICE authorizes the contractor to use government furnished vehicles, the following
requirements apply to this contract.
a. ICE will provide the contractor with government vehicles and government fleet cards (for the purchase of fuel) for the purpose of transporting aliens to and from ICE designated facilities, or alternative transportation sites. The vehicles assigned for this purpose will remain the property of
the government, and all costs associated with the operation and use of the vehicles, such as, but not
limited to, vehicle maintenance and fuel, will be covered by the government’s Fleet Management
Program.
b. The contractor agrees to be responsible for reimbursing ICE for any damage sustained by the
vehicles because of any act or omission on the part of the contractor, its employees and or persons
acting on behalf of the contractor. The contractor shall be responsible for promptly reporting any
accidents or damage to the government vehicles in accordance with any ICE policies that pertain to
reporting such damage. The contractor agrees to fully cooperate and assist ICE in making any
claims against a third party at fault for causing the property damage to the government vehicles.
In addition, the contractor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and assume financial responsibility
for any claims or litigations filed by persons sustaining personal injuries or property damage for
incidents or accidents caused by the negligent acts or omissions of the contractor, agents, or other
persons acting on behalf of the contractor. The contractor agrees to fully cooperate and assist ICE in
the defense of any claims made against ICE, and in the event of a settlement or judgment entered
against ICE for the negligent acts or omissions of the contractor employees or agents, the contractor
agrees to reimburse ICE for said settlement or adverse judgment.
d. For ICE to maintain accurate fleet records of the transportation services, the contractor shall
complete specific documentation that will be provided by ICE, to record the times of vehicle usage
for proper hourly guard reimbursement, and to record the inspection of the vehicles for damage
each time the vehicles are used.
e. The COR will provide forms to the contractor to request and authorize routine maintenance of
vehicles.
f. The contractor shall be responsible for any costs or expenses associated with the return of the
vehicles, to include towing charges, title replacement fees, or licensing expenses made necessary by
the loss of any paperwork associated with the vehicles.
rows.normalized: If ICE authorizes contractor use of government vehicles, contractor must comply with vehicle-use requirements a-f: reimbursing damage, reporting accidents, cooperating with claims, completing usage documentation, and bearing costs of vehicle return; 5 lettered requirements (a,b,d,e,f) in total.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall be responsible for promptly reporting any accidents or damage to the government vehicles in accordance with any ICE policies that pertain to reporting such damage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly report any accidents or damage to government vehicles per ICE policies.

rows.verbatim: For ICE to maintain accurate fleet records of the transportation services, the contractor shall complete specific documentation that will be provided by ICE, to record the times of vehicle usage for proper hourly guard reimbursement, and to record the inspection of the vehicles for damage each time the vehicles are used.
rows.normalized: Contractor must complete ICE-provided documentation to record vehicle usage times and inspect vehicles for damage each time used.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall be responsible for any costs or expenses associated with the return of the
vehicles, to include towing charges, title replacement fees, or licensing expenses made necessary by
the loss of any paperwork associated with the vehicles.
rows.normalized: Contractor must bear any costs or expenses tied to returning vehicles, including towing, title replacement, or licensing fees caused by lost paperwork.

rows.verbatim:
At least one vehicle used to transport detainees must be ADA equipped to safely and humanely
transport detainees with disabilities.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure at least one detainee-transport vehicle is ADA equipped for safe, humane transport of detainees with disabilities.

Transporting officers must comply with listed motor vehicle regulations: seat belt use, valid CDL, vehicle inspection, safe/humane transport, identity verification, defensive driving, no DUI, no alcohol within 8 hours before shift, USDOT driving-time limits; 9 items in total.

rows.verbatim:
If transportation
requirements change to the degree that necessitates adjustments to transportation scope and/or
contract structure, the contractor will be provided sufficient time to provide an updated price
proposal.
rows.normalized: If transportation requirements change enough to require scope/contract adjustments, contractor must be given sufficient time to submit an updated price proposal.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide on-call guard services as requested by the COR and/or ICE designated official and shall include, but is not limited to, escorting and guarding detainees to medical or doctor appointments; hearings; ICE interviews; and any other remote location requested by the COR and designated ICE official.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide on-call guard services as requested, including escorting/guarding detainees to medical appointments, hearings, ICE interviews, and other remote locations requested by COR/ICE.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide sufficient staff to escort detainees within the facility for routine appointments.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide sufficient staff to escort detainees within the facility for routine appointments.

rows.verbatim: Qualified guard personnel employed by the Contractor under their policies, procedures, and practices will perform such services.
rows.normalized: Contractor's qualified guard personnel will perform the on-call guard services under Contractor's own policies/procedures.

rows.verbatim: Upon the order of the COR and designated ICE official or in an emergency, the Contractor shall provide an officer to safeguard the detainee(s) at a medical federal facility while undergoing medical examination or treatment as either inpatient or outpatient care.
rows.normalized: If ordered by COR/ICE official or in an emergency, Contractor shall provide an officer to safeguard detainees at a medical federal facility during examination/treatment.

rows.verbatim: The detainee shall be kept under constant supervision.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall keep the detainee under constant supervision.

rows.verbatim: The numbers and frequency of these services shall vary, but to the extent possible, the COR and ICE designated officials shall notify the Contractor 48 hours in advance of such need and four hours of a schedule for the remote post to be manned.
rows.normalized: COR/ICE officials will notify the Contractor 48 hours in advance of guard service needs and provide a 4-hour schedule for staffing remote posts, creating a scheduling dependency for the Contractor.

rows.verbatim: One guard shall be authorized for such a post unless the COR specifies additional guards are required.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall staff one guard per post unless COR specifies that additional guards are required.

rows.verbatim: For safeguarding of detainees at secured community Long Term Care and Inpatient Behavioral Health Facilities, one unarmed guard shall be authorized for such posts unless COR specifies additional guards are required
rows.normalized: Contractor shall staff one unarmed guard per post at secured community Long Term Care and Inpatient Behavioral Health Facilities unless COR specifies additional guards are required.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor agrees to augment such practices as may be requested by ICE to
enhance specific requirements for security, detainee monitoring, visitation, and contraband control.
rows.normalized: Contractor must augment its guard practices as requested by ICE to enhance security, monitoring, visitation, and contraband control.

rows.verbatim: Public contact is prohibited unless authorized in advance by the COR.
rows.normalized: Public contact with detainees is prohibited unless the COR authorizes it in advance.

rows.verbatim:
All necessary meals shall be provided by the Contractor when the detainees(s) are in custody of
the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide all necessary meals while detainee(s) are in the Contractor's custody.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor remains responsible for providing security and preventing escapes.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for providing security and preventing escapes.

rows.verbatim:
The itemized
monthly invoice for such on-call guard services shall state the number of hours being billed, the
duration of the billing (times and dates to include travel to and from location being guarded) and
the names and A-numbers of the detainees who were guarded.
rows.normalized: Contractor's itemized monthly invoice for on-call guard services must state hours billed, billing duration (times/dates including travel), and detainee names and A-numbers.

rows.verbatim:
Such services shall be denoted
as a separate item on submitted invoices.
rows.normalized: Contractor must denote on-call guard services as a separate line item on submitted invoices.

rows.verbatim:
The facility plant layout and design will accommodate virtual attorney visitation with a ratio of
one booth per 100 detainees.
rows.normalized: The facility's plant layout/design will accommodate virtual attorney visitation at a ratio of one booth per 100 detainees.

rows.verbatim:
The utilized space/room/booths must be private, allowing for
confidential attorney-client conversations, and be equipped with video teleconference equipment
and/or tablet(s) permitting both visual and audio communications.
rows.normalized: The utilized space/room/booths must be private and equipped with video teleconference equipment and/or tablet(s) for visual and audio communication.

rows.verbatim: The room/booths must also have a windowed door or other mechanism that allows observation.
rows.normalized: The room/booths must have a windowed door or other mechanism allowing observation.

rows.verbatim:
While the designated space and equipment can be utilized for other purposes, it is expected that
virtual attorney visitation will be made available for at least eight (8) hours each day on weekdays
and four (4) hours per day on weekends and holidays.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make virtual attorney visitation available at least 8 hours/day on weekdays and 4 hours/day on weekends/holidays.

rows.verbatim:
When not being utilized for legal visitation, the contractor shall also use the virtual attorney
visitation rooms/booths
to facilitate virtual asylum interviews, credible fear interviews, forensic competency evaluations,
and/or DOJ EOIR Immigration Judge hearings (i.e., these rooms/booths should be set up to serve
these multiple functions).
rows.normalized: When not used for legal visitation, contractor must use the VAV rooms/booths to facilitate virtual asylum interviews, credible fear interviews, forensic competency evaluations, and/or DOJ EOIR Immigration Judge hearings.

rows.verbatim: If VAV rooms/booths are to supplement as additional court spaces, they must be in areas that can accommodate different sexes and/or classification levels.
rows.normalized: If VAV rooms/booths are used as additional court spaces, they must be located in areas accommodating different sexes and/or classification levels.

rows.verbatim: All on-call posts require at least one guard that is of the same sex as the detainee.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure each on-call post has at least one guard of the same sex as the detainee.

rows.verbatim:
Phone booths should be
soundproofed to at least the 30-35 decibel (dB) level to keep VAV conversations private.
rows.normalized: Phone booths should be soundproofed to at least 30-35 dB to keep VAV conversations private.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be prepared to begin performance and accept detainees immediately upon issuance of the NTP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must be prepared to begin performance and accept detainees immediately upon issuance of the NTP.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit in writing a Quality Control Plan (QCP) and all other plans, policies, and procedures, including those identified in the applicable ICE detention standards and ACA standards to the COR for review and concurrence prior to issuance of the NTP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit in writing a QCP and all other plans/policies/procedures to the COR for review and concurrence prior to NTP issuance.

rows.verbatim: Once written concurrence has been granted by the COR, these plans, policies, and procedures shall not be modified without the prior written approval of the COR.
rows.normalized: Once COR concurrence is granted, Contractor's plans/policies/procedures shall not be modified without prior written COR approval.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall maintain a copy of federal facility post orders for employee review within the areas of assignment and shall initiate responses to any incidents as outlined in the post orders.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain a copy of federal facility post orders for employee review and must initiate responses to incidents per those post orders.

rows.verbatim: Contractor employees shall write reports of incidents as outlined in the post orders.
rows.normalized: Contractor employees must write reports of incidents as outlined in the post orders.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will operate and control all designated points of ingress and egress on the site, such as housing units, courtrooms, medical facilities, and hold rooms.
rows.normalized: Contractor must operate and control all designated points of ingress and egress on the site, including housing units, courtrooms, medical facilities, and hold rooms.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall inspect all packages in accordance with ICE procedures.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inspect all packages in accordance with ICE procedures.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall comply with ICE security plans.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with ICE security plans.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall adhere to local operating procedures within each federal facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must adhere to local operating procedures within each federal facility.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, install, and maintain a building access control system in all ICE and/or DOJ administrative space.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, install, and maintain a building access control system in all ICE and/or DOJ administrative space.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide the government with administrative access and oversight role for system.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide the government with administrative access and an oversight role for the system.

rows.verbatim:
VAV court
rooms/booths, accommodating up to 1 detained alien, may make up
to half of the required court space with a ratio of one court space per one hundred and fifty (150)
detainees.
rows.normalized: VAV court rooms/booths (up to 1 detainee each) may comprise up to half of required court space, at a ratio of one court space per 150 detainees.

rows.verbatim:
Performance includes, but is not limited to, preliminary fitness determination and training
documentation for an adequate number of federal facility staff.
rows.normalized: Contractor performance includes, at minimum, preliminary fitness determination and training documentation for an adequate number of federal facility staff.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will supervise, observe, and protect aliens from sexual abuse, discrimination,
corporal punishment, personal injury, property damage, harassment, or violation of aliens’ civil
rights.
rows.normalized: Contractor will supervise, observe, and protect aliens from sexual abuse, discrimination, corporal punishment, personal injury, property damage, harassment, or civil rights violations.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have a zero-tolerance policy for incidents of sexual abuse or assault.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall have a zero-tolerance policy for incidents of sexual abuse or assault.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall attempt to detect anyone attempting to gain unauthorized access to the site(s)
identified in this contract and notify both ICE and local law enforcement.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall attempt to detect unauthorized access attempts at contract sites and notify ICE and local law enforcement.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will provide supervision of all aliens in all areas, including supervision in medical,
housing, and activity areas, to permit detention officers to hear and respond promptly to
emergencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor will provide supervision of all aliens in all areas, including medical, housing, and activity areas, so officers can hear and respond promptly to emergencies.

rows.verbatim:
This shall include providing medical housing unit security officer with video
surveillance unit to view all patients’ rooms.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide medical housing unit security officer with a video surveillance unit to view all patients' rooms.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have direct supervision of each
housing unit.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall have direct supervision of each housing unit.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall comply with the requirements applicable to detention facilities contained in
Subpart A of the DHS PREA Standards, specifically §115.13, including the development of alien
supervision guidelines that are reviewed annually, as outlined in Attachment -- Prison Rape
Elimination Act Regulations.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall comply with DHS PREA Standards Subpart A §115.13, including developing alien supervision guidelines reviewed annually.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall ensure video surveillance of hallways, exits, and common areas.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure video surveillance of hallways, exits, and common areas.

rows.verbatim: Additionally, surveillance systems shall be installed and updated in accordance with DHS PREA §115.18(b).
rows.normalized: Surveillance systems must be installed and updated per DHS PREA §115.18(b).

rows.verbatim: The system shall have a network time protocol (NTP) Server, like Time Machines TM-1000, as an element of the VSS solution to ensure system timing accuracy.
rows.normalized: The VSS system must include an NTP server for timing accuracy.

rows.verbatim: All network devices shall be set to periodically communicate with the NTP server to adjust for timing inaccuracies.
rows.normalized: All network devices must periodically communicate with the NTP server.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide and install a minimum of an 8-hour emergency power solution for all video surveillance system (VSS) hardware.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide and install at least an 8-hour emergency power solution for all VSS hardware.

rows.verbatim: If emergency power is available, via generator, a battery backup must be provided to cover transfer time, minimum of 30 minutes.
rows.normalized: If emergency power is via generator, contractor must provide a battery backup covering at least 30 minutes of transfer time.

rows.verbatim:
Network video
recorder (NVR) hard disk drives used for video storage, such as the Western Digital ITB-
10TB (a.k.a. Purple Surveillance Storage), must be built to withstand continuous read/write
activity.
rows.normalized: NVR hard disk drives used for video storage must be built to withstand continuous read/write activity.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor will determine the storage capacity of the NVR(s) based on the following criteria:
• Quantity of cameras
• Period of motion activated recording per camera
• Frames-per-Second (fps) for each camera
• A minimum of 90 days of storage for each camera
• NVR servers shall have failover capabilities and redundancy to ensure continuous function in the event an NVR experiences a failure
• Workstations to export video evidence in open format such as audio-video interleave or QuickTime Movie (e.g. avi or mov) and provide chain of custody
• H.265 or better compression
rows.normalized: Contractor must determine NVR storage capacity based on listed criteria (camera quantity, recording period, fps, minimum 90 days storage, failover/redundancy, export workstations, H.265+ compression).

rows.verbatim:
NVR servers shall have failover capabilities and redundancy to ensure continuous
function in the event an NVR experiences a failure
rows.normalized: NVR servers must have failover capabilities and redundancy to ensure continuous function if an NVR fails.

rows.verbatim:
Cameras must provide 100% coverage of perimeter, detention and high-
security areas.
rows.normalized: Cameras must provide 100% coverage of perimeter, detention, and high-security areas.

rows.verbatim:
In detention holding cells, cameras will be mounted such that video is not seen
or recorded in the toilet/privacy area.
rows.normalized: Cameras in detention holding cells will be mounted so video is not seen or recorded in the toilet/privacy area.

rows.verbatim: All cameras will have 2-megapixel or better resolution.
rows.normalized: All cameras will have 2-megapixel or better resolution.

rows.verbatim:
All exterior cameras shall have an
infrared (IR) cut-filter and/or IR night time illuminator either built in or added as an
accessory.
rows.normalized: All exterior cameras shall have an IR cut-filter and/or IR night-time illuminator, built in or added.

rows.verbatim:
All exterior cameras shall be environmentally protected based on the prevailing
weather conditions for the geographical area and as prescribed by the camera manufacturer.
rows.normalized: All exterior cameras shall be environmentally protected per prevailing weather conditions and manufacturer specifications.

rows.verbatim: PTZ cameras shall not be programmed on an area tour to provide 100% coverage.
rows.normalized: PTZ cameras shall not be programmed on an area tour to provide 100% coverage.

rows.verbatim: These cameras shall only be utilized for additional monitoring capability.
rows.normalized: PTZ cameras shall only be used for additional monitoring capability.

rows.verbatim:
Cameras shall be positioned to prevent tampering which includes installing in fixed, tamper and vandal
resistant enclosures.
rows.normalized: Cameras shall be positioned to prevent tampering, including installation in fixed, tamper- and vandal-resistant enclosures.

rows.verbatim:
Cameras installed in detention areas (housing area, holding, etc.) will be
detention grade.
rows.normalized: Cameras installed in detention areas will be detention grade.

rows.verbatim:
Monitors shall have the appropriate built-in video and management ports based on the VSS
system design requirements and shall not have any wireless connection (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth
etc.) capability enabled.
rows.normalized: Monitors shall have appropriate built-in video/management ports per VSS design and shall not have wireless connectivity enabled.

rows.verbatim:
Wall mounted monitors shall be installed using a premium type full-
motion wall bracket to provide tilt, swivel and arm extension capabilities, unless specified
differently by ICE.
rows.normalized: Wall mounted monitors shall be installed with a premium full-motion wall bracket (tilt/swivel/arm extension) unless ICE specifies otherwise.

rows.verbatim:
For multiple monitor installations videos shall be organized for security
personnel to easily follow movement through the facility from one camera to the next in a
smooth flowing fashion without having to bounce back and forth among monitors.
rows.normalized: For multiple monitor installations, video shall be organized so security personnel can follow movement smoothly across cameras.

rows.verbatim:
VSS
workstations and decoders shall not exceed the manufacture's recommended number of
displayed cameras or connected monitors.
rows.normalized: VSS workstations and decoders shall not exceed the manufacturer's recommended number of displayed cameras or connected monitors.

rows.verbatim:
All monitors shall be capable of viewing the specified number of camera views listed below at 30 fps (real time) with no lag:
• Monitors for general area observation shall be capable of 16 camera views per monitor.
• A minimum of 27-32” monitors shall be utilized for guard stations and other areas where size restrictions will not allow 42-50” monitors. Monitors shall be capable of 8 camera views per monitor
• 22-26” monitors shall be utilized for VSS workstations, alarm call-up, or specific spot area monitors.
Monitors shall be capable of 1-4 camera views per monitor.
rows.normalized: All monitors must support specified camera view counts at 30fps: general area 16 views/monitor, 27-32in guard station monitors 8 views/monitor, 22-26in workstation monitors 1-4 views/monitor.

rows.verbatim: Cameras should capture video with a minimum resolution of 40 pixels-per-foot (PPF) at the target distance.
rows.normalized: Cameras should capture video at a minimum of 40 PPF resolution at target distance.

rows.verbatim: A minimum of 27-32” monitors shall be utilized for guard stations and other areas where size restrictions will not allow 42-50” monitors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use 27-32” monitors for guard stations and other size-restricted areas.

rows.verbatim: Monitors shall be capable of 8 camera views per monitor
rows.normalized: Monitors used for guard stations must be capable of 8 camera views per monitor.

rows.verbatim: 22-26” monitors shall be utilized for VSS workstations, alarm call-up, or specific spot area monitors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use 22-26” monitors for VSS workstations, alarm call-up, or spot area monitors.

rows.verbatim: All AC voltage powered devices shall be connected to a centrally located uninterruptable power supply (UPS) in the designated IT/LAN equipment and frame/closet rooms.
rows.normalized: All AC-powered devices must be connected to a centrally located UPS in designated IT/LAN rooms.

rows.verbatim: As part of the VSS package, the contractor shall provide a rack mount keyboard-video-mouse (KVM) console with appropriate cabling for connection to each NVR and matrix (if used), or properly configured network client with remote access (on the dedicated VSS network), for video and software management and maintenance.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a rack mount KVM console (or configured network client) with cabling for each NVR/matrix as part of the VSS package.

rows.verbatim: Man-down and duress system for officer safety shall be integrated with VSS.
rows.normalized: The man-down and duress system must be integrated with VSS.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall have warranty all contractor supplied components, workmanship and/or systems for a (minimum) period of 12 months from the date of Government acceptance.
rows.normalized: Contractor must warranty all contractor-supplied components, workmanship, and systems for at least 12 months from Government acceptance.

rows.verbatim: After the one-year base warranty period the contractor shall include four one-year option periods for technical services, support, testing, maintenance and repair of the system and components installed in this PWS.
rows.normalized: After the base warranty year, contractor must include four one-year option periods for technical services/support/testing/maintenance/repair.

rows.verbatim: In the event any contractor-supplied equipment, component, part fails within the specified warranty period; the contractor shall immediately replace or repair the item within 24 hours at no additional cost to the Government.
rows.normalized: If contractor-supplied equipment fails within warranty, contractor must replace/repair within 24 hours at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim: If the contractor is unable to rectify the issue(s) within the allotted time, the contractor shall be liable for all costs incurred by the Government to correct the issue(s).
rows.normalized: If contractor cannot rectify issues within the allotted time, contractor must be liable for the Government's correction costs.

rows.verbatim: Any critical component that becomes inoperable must be replaced or repaired.
rows.normalized: Any inoperable critical component must be replaced or repaired.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall implement a maintenance program for all security systems.
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement a maintenance program for all security systems.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall conduct quarterly, semi-annual, and annual maintenance at the facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct quarterly, semi-annual, and annual maintenance at the facility.

rows.verbatim: The contractor is responsible for the scheduling and execution of preventive maintenance on all ICE VSS electronic security equipment and systems.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for scheduling and executing preventive maintenance on all ICE VSS equipment.

rows.verbatim: Each equipment room will contain a building-grounded, grounding buss bar which will be utilized for equipment rack and panel grounding connectivity.
rows.normalized: Each equipment room must contain a building-grounded grounding buss bar for rack/panel grounding.

rows.verbatim:
Quarterly:
• Software updates
• Firmware updates
• Patches
rows.normalized: Quarterly maintenance must include software updates, firmware updates, and patches.

rows.verbatim: Prior to testing any VSS equipment the contractor shall notify the ICE OPR Point of Contact.
rows.normalized: Prior to testing VSS equipment, contractor must notify the ICE OPR Point of Contact.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall perform on-site functional evaluations of existing security systems at the identified ICE facility per manufacturer’s specifications, and if necessary, shall recommend methods of remediation to make the system fully operational per manufacturer and DHS/ICE specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform on-site functional evaluations per manufacturer specs and, if necessary, recommend remediation methods.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall be solely responsible for conducting any repair or replacement work required to maintain the systems in the condition prescribed by the original equipment manufacturer’s recommended guidelines and/or warranty requirements (where the warranty remains in force).
rows.normalized: Contractor is solely responsible for repair/replacement work to maintain systems per OEM guidelines/warranty requirements.

rows.verbatim: If any components are found to need repair or replacement, the contractor shall be responsible for following all procedures listed in this PWS.
rows.normalized: If components need repair/replacement, contractor must follow all PWS procedures.

rows.verbatim: Failure to follow any procedures listed in this PWS shall be done at the contractor’s risk.
rows.normalized: Any failure to follow PWS procedures is at the contractor's risk.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall perform a complete inspection and functional test of the VSS System, verifying 100% functionality, per manufacturers and DHS/ICE standards, of all system capabilities to include, but not limited to: pan, tilt, tilt, zoom features, recorders, monitors, controllers, fiber optic transceivers, and connections associated with the system.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform complete inspection/functional test of VSS verifying 100% functionality, including pan/tilt/zoom, recorders, monitors, controllers, fiber optic transceivers, connections.

rows.verbatim:
Maintenance shall be performed at each location semi-
annually.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform maintenance at each location semi-annually.

rows.verbatim: Maintenance visits shall be scheduled no less than 90 calendar days apart.
rows.normalized: Maintenance visits must be scheduled no less than 90 calendar days apart.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide on-site software maintenance support, software and firmware upgrades, software patches, virus protection, and system configuration changes, as necessary.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide on-site software maintenance support, upgrades, patches, virus protection, and configuration changes as needed.

rows.verbatim: This support shall start upon successful completion of the Substantial Completion Inspection (SCI) and include support for the Video Management Software System components.
rows.normalized: Software maintenance support must start upon successful SCI completion and cover Video Management Software System components.

rows.verbatim: The contractor SHALL NOT use Remote Desktop connections, (e.g., Microsoft’s Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), without the use of an authentication method that employs secure authentication (two-factor, encrypted, key exchange).
rows.normalized: Contractor must not use Remote Desktop connections without secure authentication (two-factor, encrypted, key exchange).

rows.verbatim: Use of removable media for maintenance purposes shall adhere to the policies and procedures established by the System Owners.
rows.normalized: Use of removable media for maintenance must adhere to System Owner policies/procedures.

rows.verbatim:
Semi-Annually:
• Preventive maintenance
• Camera cleaning
• Head-end rack equipment cleaning (Racks, Workstations, Servers, PoE switch, UPS)
rows.normalized: Semi-annual maintenance must include preventive maintenance, camera cleaning, and head-end rack equipment cleaning.

rows.verbatim:
Annually:
• Equipment functionality testing of all equipment and devices
rows.normalized: Annual maintenance must include equipment functionality testing of all equipment and devices.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall maintain an incident log as part of the software maintenance program,
recording therein all deviations from normative operations, and all corrective actions taken.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain an incident log recording all deviations and corrective actions as part of the software maintenance program.

rows.verbatim:
The incident log shall be submitted to ICE/OPR upon detection of anomalies, quarterly, and
at the end of the contract period.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the incident log to ICE/OPR upon detection of anomalies, quarterly, and at contract end.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall perform preventative
maintenance on all VSS equipment as specified by ICE and the manufacturers and DHS/ICE
specifications and industry best practices.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform preventative maintenance on all VSS equipment per ICE, manufacturer, and DHS/ICE specifications and industry best practices.

rows.verbatim:
Preventative maintenance functions shall include
but are not limited to, focusing and back-focusing of cameras, cleaning of recording devices
(servers, NVRs, DVRs), switches and verification of controller programming.
rows.normalized: Contractor's preventative maintenance functions must include, at minimum: focusing/back-focusing cameras, cleaning recording devices (servers, NVRs, DVRs), switches, and verification of controller programming.

rows.verbatim:
The
contractor shall verify the video transmission system, and that any signal or control cabling

rows.normalized: Contractor employees shall provide first aid and CPR when necessary.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure the following medical personnel maintain valid, active, permanent, full, independent, and unrestricted credentials in accordance with State law:
a. Licensed Independent Provider (LIP): An LIP is defined as an individual, as permitted by law and regulation, and by the organization, to provide care and services without direction or supervision within the scope of the individual’s license and consistent with the privileges granted by the organization.
1) Physicians: Medical Doctor (MD), Doctor of Osteopathy (DO);
2) Dentists: Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS), Doctor of Dental Medicine (DMD);
3) Psychologists: Doctor of Psychology (PsyD or PhD) in Clinical or Counseling Psychology from a graduate program in Psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association:
i. At least, two (2) years of supervised experience in Clinical, Counseling, or Health Psychology; and
ii. Meet requirements for inclusion in the National Registry of Psychologist Providers if graduated after 1 January 1982.
4) Social Workers: Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) requirements:
i. Successful completion of a Master of Social Work (MSW) from a graduate program accredited by Council on Social Work Education (CSWE); and
ii. The clinical social worker license must be the highest clinically independent licensed clinical social work designated by the licensing board where it was received; and
iii. A minimum of three years post-independent licensure clinical experience providing independent clinical assessment, diagnosing using the DSM-V-TR (and any future DSM publications) and developing clinical treatment plans without supervision; and
iv. Provide documentation/transcripts demonstrating clinical work within completed graduate program requested; and
v. Must complete 20 hours of Continuing Education Units (CEUs) annually approved by the American Psychological Association (APA) or National Association of Social Workers (NASW); Additional CEU hours may be obtained by another sponsoring equivalent; and
vi. Shall maintain membership with licensing board associated with clinical license and submit required completion of CEUs to the licensing board annually as required; Membership with the state or territory clinical licensing board is required.

5) Ensures MedPAR/referral entries related to emergency department or hospital admissions
must be entered into the MPv2S within one business day after the detainee is discharged.
6) Serves as the primary POC that collaborates with the FMC to resolve alien number
discrepancies between the MPv2S and Enforce system.
7) Responsible for arranging custody transport for detainee authorized MedPAR/referrals
community provider appointments.
8) Responsible for sending authorizations of MedPARs/referrals to community providers or
their billing partners.
9) Responsible for providing and maintaining a current comprehensive list of hospitals and
community providers with data points as specified and provide a copy to the FMC initially
and when updates are made.
10) Serves as the primary contact for FMCs, other IHSC staff, community providers, and other
applicable stakeholders related to adjudication of MedPARs/referrals, medical record
requests, billing and medical claims adjudication.
11) Responsible for responding to medical referral/billing/claims, or authorization
communications received for timely resolution (mail, emails, or phone calls) and
collaborating with the FMC as applicable.
12) Responds and assists community providers with complaints related to denied claims by
gathering the following information to review with the FMC within three business days.
rows.normalized: Contractor's designated MedPAR/referral point of contact must perform 12 listed responsibilities (recruitment letters, SME/training role, ensuring MedPARs completed, timely adjudication, entries within 1 business day, resolving alien number discrepancies, arranging transport, sending authorizations, maintaining provider list, serving as primary contact, responding to communications, and gathering complaint info within 3 business days); item 12 further lists 14 sub-items (i-xiv) of data to gather, not shown here.

rows.verbatim:
12) Responds and assists community providers with complaints related to denied claims by gathering the following information to review with the FMC within three business days.
i. Provider Name
ii. Provider phone number
iii. Provider email address
iv. Point of contact first/last name
v. TAX ID# or EIN
vi. Billing NPI#
vii. Illegal Alien First Name
viii. Illegal Alien Last Name
ix. Alien ID#
x. Date of Birth
xi. Date(s) of Service
xii. MedPAR Specialty: (ER, In-Pt etc.)
xiii. Denial code from Explanation of Benefit (EOB).
xiv. IHSC issued authorization number if applicable
rows.normalized: Point of contact must gather 14 specified data items and review denied-claim complaints with the FMC within three business days.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must ensure adequate supply of medication(s) for release, transfer, or removal of a
detainee in accordance with detention standards or additional medication supply requirements (e.g.,
court mandate minimum supply, ICE mission requirements).
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure adequate medication supply for detainee release, transfer, or removal.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be given advance notice by ICE/ERO prior to the release, transfer, or removal of a
detainee, so that medical staff may determine and provide for any medical needs associated with the transfer,
release, or removal.
rows.normalized: Contractor is to receive advance notice from ICE/ERO before detainee release/transfer/removal, a government dependency affecting Contractor medical planning.

rows.verbatim:
In the event ICE/ERO is transferring a detainee to a less than 72-hour facility for ultimate release or
removal, the Contractor shall fill the prescription(s) at a network pharmacy and ensure an adequate
supply of medication(s) for both transfer and release is provided to the detainee.
rows.normalized: If ICE/ERO transfers a detainee to a less-than-72-hour facility, Contractor shall fill prescriptions at a network pharmacy and ensure adequate medication supply for both transfer and release.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must notify ICE (through the COR) and the IHSC FMC of detainees with serious
medical conditions immediately upon identification of conditions and no more than 24 hours of
identification of the case.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify ICE/COR and IHSC FMC of detainees with serious medical conditions immediately, and no later than 24 hours after identification.

rows.verbatim:
If the Contractor determines that an ICE detainee has a medical condition which renders that person
unacceptable for detention under this agreement (for example, condition needing life support,
uncontrollable violence, or serious mental health condition), the Contractor shall notify their FMC,
Behavioral Health Case Manager (BHCM) and ICE.
rows.normalized: If Contractor determines a detainee has a condition making detention unacceptable, Contractor shall notify FMC, BHCM, and ICE.

rows.verbatim:
Upon such notification, the Contractor shall allow ICE reasonable time to make the proper
arrangements for further disposition of the detainee.
rows.normalized: After notifying ICE, Contractor shall allow ICE reasonable time to arrange further disposition of the detainee.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor should expect to be requested and attest to ICE that the detainee is medically
cleared for transportation and advise ICE of the necessary precautions and equipment required for
such transportation.
rows.normalized: Contractor is expected to attest to ICE that a detainee is medically cleared for transport and advise on precautions/equipment needed.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall identify, track, record and maintain a list of all detainees identified as having a
serious mental disorder or condition and/or who are determined to be incompetent by an
immigration judge until removal or release.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify, track, record, and maintain a list of detainees with serious mental disorders/incompetency determinations until removal or release.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall complete the IHSC Form 883 and submit it to IHSC FMC/Behavioral Health Case
Manager (BHCM) when the detainee has been identified.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall complete and submit IHSC Form 883 to FMC/BHCM upon identification of the detainee.

rows.verbatim:
Notification to the FMC and the COR shall occur as soon as practicable but no later than
72 hours after identification of detained individuals with a serious mental disorder or condition.
rows.normalized: Notification to FMC and COR shall occur as soon as practicable, no later than 72 hours after identification of an SMI detainee.

rows.verbatim:
In addition, a list shall be provided to the COR and IHSC FMC on a weekly basis and include name,
A#, date of arrival, diagnosis (es), presence or absence of suicidality, specific symptoms exhibited
by detainee that meets criteria of a Serious Mental Disorder or Condition, list of prescribed
psychotropic medication with dosage, date when IHSC Form 883 was completed and submitted to
IHSC FMC, and details for Safe Release Planning pursuant to ICE Directive 11063.2:
Identification, Communication, Recordkeeping, and Safe Release Planning for Detained Individuals
with Serious Mental Disorders or Conditions and/or Who Are Determined To Be Incompetent By
An Immigration Judge.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a weekly list to COR/IHSC FMC including name, A#, arrival date, diagnosis, suicidality status, symptoms, medications, Form 883 date, and Safe Release Planning details.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide semi-annual SMI training to clinic staff, in accordance with current
ICE policies and procedures in coordination with IHSC, and communicated through the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide semi-annual SMI training to clinic staff.

rows.verbatim:
In the event of a medical emergency, the Contractor shall ensure immediate response and provide
necessary emergency medical treatment, including initial on-site stabilization and off-site transport
to an appropriate emergent care facility, as needed.
rows.normalized: In a medical emergency, Contractor shall ensure immediate response and provide necessary emergency treatment including stabilization and transport.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall notify ICE as soon as practical regarding the nature of the transferred detainee’s illness
or injury and the type of treatment provided.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall notify ICE as soon as practical about the nature of the detainee's illness/injury and treatment provided.

rows.verbatim:
All emergency medical services provided off-site require an authorized MedPAR/referral
to be entered within the MPv2S within one business day upon return from the hospital.
rows.normalized: All off-site emergency medical services require an authorized MedPAR/referral entered into MPv2S within one business day of return from hospital.

rows.verbatim: At no time shall the Contractor or detainee incur financial liability related to such services.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall never allow itself or the detainee to incur financial liability for these emergency services.

rows.verbatim:
Therefore, the Contractor shall provide direct, ready access to licensed ambulance services capable of
advanced life support (ALS) and basic life support (BLS).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide direct, ready access to licensed ALS/BLS ambulance services.

rows.verbatim:
Ambulances must be available for transport to local hospitals or medical facilities as
needed 24/7.
rows.normalized: Ambulances (provided by Contractor) must be available 24/7 for transport to local hospitals/facilities.

rows.verbatim:
EMS personnel must be licensed and maintain current certifications in CPR, first aid,
and relevant EMS protocols.
rows.normalized: Contractor's EMS personnel must be licensed and maintain current CPR/first aid/EMS certifications.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure all EMS equipment and supplies are
maintained, inspected, and available for immediate use.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure EMS equipment/supplies are maintained, inspected, and available for immediate use.

rows.verbatim: Ambulances must be equipped in accordance with applicable federal standards.
rows.normalized: Ambulances (Contractor-provided) must be equipped per applicable federal standards.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish effective relationships with local community providers.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall establish effective relationships with local community providers.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure comprehensive fire suppression and emergency response services are
available 24/7. Services shall include, but are not limited to:
• Deployment of trained and certified personnel capable of responding to fire emergencies,
hazardous material incidents, and related emergencies.
• Operation and maintenance of fire suppression equipment, including fire trucks, extinguishers,
sprinkler systems, and other necessary apparatus.
• Implementation of rapid response protocols to ensure timely arrival and effective mitigation of
fire and emergency incidents.
• Conducting regular fire safety inspections, drills, and training for facility staff.
• Coordination with local emergency services and authorities as required.
• Documentation and reporting of all incidents, responses, and maintenance activities in accordance with applicable regulations and standards.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure 24/7 fire suppression/emergency response services, including at minimum: trained personnel deployment, equipment operation/maintenance, rapid response protocols, fire safety inspections/drills/training, coordination with local emergency services, and documentation/reporting of incidents.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide monthly reports to the COR on emergency response, response times,
and incidents.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide monthly reports to the COR on emergency response, response times, and incidents.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall furnish a 24 hours/seven days per week emergency medical/dental/mental
health care contact list which must include local hospitals and other off-site specialty care providers
to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish a 24/7 emergency medical/dental/mental health contact list, including local hospitals and off-site specialty providers, to the COR.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure detainees always have access to an off-site emergency
medical provider.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure detainees always have access to an off-site emergency medical provider.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must maintain a facility emergency evacuation procedure guide that includes
evacuation of any patients currently housed in a medical/mental health housing area, including any
isolation rooms as well as other special housing areas within the facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain a facility emergency evacuation procedure guide covering evacuation of medical/mental health housing areas, isolation rooms, and special housing areas.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must
provide training on all emergency plans to the on-site medical staff, both initially and annually after
hire.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide training on all emergency plans to on-site medical staff initially and annually thereafter.

rows.verbatim:
Upon order of the COR or designated ICE officer, or in an emergency, the Contractor shall take
custody of and safeguard detainee(s) at a hospital or clinic when the detainee(s) is undergoing
medical examination.
rows.normalized: Upon COR/ICE order or in an emergency, Contractor shall take custody of and safeguard detainees at a hospital/clinic during medical examination.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor employee will remain on duty until relieved by another Contractor employee.
rows.normalized: Contractor employee will remain on duty until relieved by another Contractor employee.

rows.verbatim:
24-hour custody shall be maintained, with constant visual observation when
practicable.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain 24-hour custody with constant visual observation when practicable.

rows.verbatim:
The detainees shall not use the telephones unless the Contractor receives prior approval
from the COR or other designated ICE official.
rows.normalized: Detainees may not use telephones unless Contractor first receives COR/ICE approval.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor employees shall not fraternize with clinic/hospital staff or with casual visitors to the
clinic/hospital.
rows.normalized: Contractor employees shall not fraternize with clinic/hospital staff or casual visitors.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor is obligated to relay messages as requested by the detainee to the COR or other
designated ICE official.
rows.normalized: Contractor is obligated to relay detainee-requested messages to the COR or designated ICE official.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall comply with the applicable ICE detention standard covering Terminal Illness
and Death, in the event of a detainee injury or death.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall comply with the applicable ICE detention standard on Terminal Illness and Death upon detainee injury or death.

rows.verbatim:
In the event of a detainee death, the Contractor
shall immediately notify the FMC and COR or ICE designated official and submit a written report
within 24 hours.
rows.normalized: Upon a detainee death, Contractor shall immediately notify FMC/COR/ICE and submit a written report within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall fingerprint the deceased.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall fingerprint the deceased.

rows.verbatim:
Staff members performing the fingerprinting
shall date and sign the fingerprint card to ensure that a positive identification has
been made and file the card in the detainee’s file.
rows.normalized: Contractor staff performing fingerprinting shall date and sign the fingerprint card and file it in the detainee's file.

rows.verbatim:
Personal property of the deceased shall be
inventoried, and release is to be coordinated with ICE to the designated family member, the nearest
of kin, or the Consular Officer of the detainee’s country of legal residence.
rows.normalized: Deceased detainee's personal property shall be inventoried and its release coordinated with ICE to family/kin/consular officer.

rows.verbatim:
If death is due to violence, accident surrounded by unusual or questionable circumstances or is
sudden and the deceased has not been under immediate medical supervision, the Contractor shall
notify the coroner of the local jurisdiction to request a review of the case, and if necessary,
examination of the body.
rows.normalized: If death is violent, accidental/unusual, or sudden without prior medical supervision, Contractor shall notify the local coroner to request case review and possible examination.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall establish, and report to the COR, coroner notification procedures outlining
such issues as performance of an autopsy, who will perform the autopsy, obtaining state-approved
death certificates, and local transportation of the body.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall establish and report to COR coroner notification procedures covering autopsy performance, death certificates, and body transportation.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor, in coordination with the COR or Designated Service Official, shall ensure the body
is turned over to the designated family member, the nearest of kin, or the Consular Officer of the
detainee’s country of legal residence.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure, in coordination with COR/Designated Service Official, the body is turned over to family/kin/consular officer.

rows.verbatim:
When an autopsy is requested, the
Contractor shall communicate the request to the FMC.
rows.normalized: When an autopsy is requested, Contractor shall communicate the request to the FMC.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor must obtain an invoice from the autopsy provider and, if applicable, provide a complete
recruitment letter and submit it to the FMC.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain autopsy provider invoice and, if applicable, provide/submit a complete recruitment letter to FMC.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall release all information relevant to the detainee death investigation to ICE (e.g.,
medical information, incident reports, eyewitness accounts, video footage) upon request.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall release all detainee death investigation information to ICE upon request.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will adhere to all infectious disease prevention and management guidelines,
treatment, and reporting as required by local, state, and federal public health authorities.
rows.normalized: Contractor will adhere to all infectious disease prevention/management guidelines, treatment, and reporting required by public health authorities.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor should follow infectious disease and standard precautions as well as isolation, cohorting,
and quarantine recommendations as outlined in the most current guidance set forth by the IHSC
Public Health, Safety, and Preparedness Unit.
rows.normalized: Contractor should follow infectious disease/standard precautions and isolation/cohorting/quarantine recommendations per current IHSC guidance.

rows.verbatim:
In order to prevent the spread of airborne infectious disease or cross contamination of zones within
the facility, the HVAC system in the intake screening area shall be designed to exhaust to the
exterior and prevent air exchange between the intake screening area and any other area within the
facility (see CDC guidelines http://www.cdc.gov/tb/publications/guidelines/Correctional.htm).
rows.normalized: The HVAC system in the intake screening area shall be designed to exhaust exterior and prevent air exchange with other areas, to prevent infectious disease spread.

rows.verbatim:
Airborne Isolation Infection (AII) rooms (e.g., negative pressure rooms) must be inspected annually
by a certified technician, or per manufacturer recommendations, to ensure proper functionality and
quality control.
rows.normalized: AII (negative pressure) rooms must be inspected annually by a certified technician or per manufacturer recommendations.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will ensure that there is adequate space and equipment to provide medical intake
screening including tuberculosis (TB) screening within the intake processing area.
rows.normalized: Contractor will ensure adequate space/equipment for medical intake screening including TB screening in the intake processing area.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will perform onsite TB screening as part of the routine intake screening, which must
be completed within 12 hours of detainee admission.
rows.normalized: Contractor will perform onsite TB screening during routine intake, completed within 12 hours of admission.

rows.verbatim:
TB screening will include, at a minimum, both TB symptom screening and testing for TB infection and/or disease using any Center for Disease
Control and Prevention (CDC) approved method or chest x-ray.
rows.normalized: TB screening will include at a minimum both symptom screening and testing for TB infection/disease via a CDC-approved method or chest x-ray.

rows.verbatim:
Detainees who have symptoms suggestive of TB disease will be immediately placed in an airborne
infection isolation room and promptly evaluated for suspected TB disease.
rows.normalized: If a detainee has symptoms suggestive of TB, Contractor will immediately place them in an airborne infection isolation room and promptly evaluate for TB.

rows.verbatim:
Detainees who are initially tested using a test for TB infection [TB skin test (TST) or interferon
gamma release assay (IGRA)], and the results are positive according to criteria, but have no
symptoms suggestive of TB disease, must be evaluated with a chest radiograph within 5 days of the
notification of a positive result.
rows.normalized: If a detainee tests positive for TB infection (TST/IGRA) without TB symptoms, must be evaluated with chest radiograph within 5 days of positive result notification.

rows.verbatim:
Detainees who are identified with confirmed or suspected active TB (e.g., symptoms or chest
radiograph suggestive of TB) will be placed in a functional airborne infection isolation room and
managed in accordance with the applicable standard and all applicable CDC guidelines:
rows.normalized: If a detainee is identified with confirmed/suspected active TB, will be placed in a functional airborne infection isolation room and managed per applicable standards/CDC guidelines.

rows.verbatim: The facility will have an alternative non-punitive process in place for detainees who refuse the TB screening assessment.
rows.normalized: The facility must maintain an alternative non-punitive process for detainees who refuse TB screening.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will notify IHSC and the local health department of all detainees with confirmed or
suspected TB disease, including detainees with clinical or radiographic evidence suggestive of TB.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify IHSC and the local health department of all detainees with confirmed or suspected TB disease.

rows.verbatim:
Notification shall occur within one working day of identifying a detainee with confirmed or
suspected TB disease.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify within one working day of identifying a detainee with confirmed or suspected TB disease.

rows.verbatim:
Notification to local health departments shall identify the detainee as being in
ICE custody and shall include the ICE detainee number and other identifying information.
rows.normalized: Notification to local health departments must identify detainee's ICE custody status and include the ICE detainee number and other identifying information.

rows.verbatim:
For detainees with confirmed or suspected TB disease, the Contractor will coordinate with IHSC and
the local health department to facilitate release planning and referrals for continuity of care prior to
release.
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate with IHSC and the local health department on release planning and referrals for detainees with confirmed/suspected TB.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will evaluate detainees annually for symptoms consistent with TB within one year
of the previously documented TB evaluation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must annually evaluate detainees for TB symptoms within one year of prior TB evaluation.

rows.verbatim:
For detainees initially screened with a TST or IGRA
with a negative result, annual evaluation will include testing with the same method as previously
used.
rows.normalized: If a detainee's initial TB screening was TST/IGRA negative, the annual evaluation must use the same testing method.

rows.verbatim:
When the Contractor conducts initial TB screening using any CDC-recommended
method, including onsite radiology services (e.g., mobile radiology), the cost shall be
included in the bed rate.
rows.normalized: If Contractor conducts initial TB screening including onsite radiology services, the cost shall be included in the bed rate.

rows.verbatim: If the Contractor utilizes offsite radiology services for TB screening confirmation, the Contractor must follow IHSC’s third-party claim process (MEDPAR entry or waiver) to obtain reimbursement.
rows.normalized: If Contractor uses offsite radiology services for TB screening confirmation, it must follow IHSC's third-party claim process for reimbursement.

rows.verbatim:
When the Contractor opts to purchase x-ray equipment (and all other associated
costs) to utilize chest radiology for the purpose of TB screening, the Contractor will be
financially responsible for purchasing the equipment, associated equipment servicing costs,
as well as any federal or state mandated radiology certification costs, to include dosimetry.
rows.normalized: If Contractor opts to purchase x-ray equipment for chest radiology, Contractor is financially responsible for equipment purchase, servicing costs, and required certification costs including dosimetry.

rows.verbatim:
Additionally, the Contractor is financially responsible for all associated radiology staffing
service costs, and diagnostic interpretation costs.
rows.normalized: Contractor is financially responsible for radiology staffing service costs and diagnostic interpretation costs.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall implement all general housekeeping and environmental cleaning and
disinfection requirements consistent with the Environmental Health and Safety sections of the
applicable standard in all areas where medical, dental, mental health, and intake medical screening
services are rendered, including routine and terminal cleaning of medical housing and medical
isolation units based on 24/7/365 needs.
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement housekeeping/environmental cleaning and disinfection requirements per the applicable standard's EH&S sections in all medical service areas, 24/7/365.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall implement an internal review and medical quality assurance program for the
purpose of maintaining operations in accordance with the applicable ICE detention standards, ACA
standards, and any other accreditation standards , which refers to formal certification by authorized
organizations confirming compliance with established health care service standards.
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement an internal review and medical QA program to maintain compliance with ICE, ACA, and other accreditation standards.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall conduct a quality improvement / quality of care review consistent with an
established quality improvement (medical quality management) program and interfacing with the
IHSC quality improvement program (available upon request) consistent with federal, state, and
local laws.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct a quality improvement/quality of care review consistent with an established QI program, interfacing with IHSC's QI program, per applicable laws.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a continuous quality improvement plan/ medical quality assurance
plan and annually to the FMC for review.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a continuous quality improvement/medical QA plan annually to the FMC for review.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor ensures quality health care delivery and accountability in compliance with detention
standards through a continuous quality improvement (CQI) system that includes risk management,
patient safety, and health services delivery quality assurance programs.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure quality health care delivery and accountability via a CQI system including risk management, patient safety, and QA programs.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor is required to report all incidents, according to IHSC incident reporting criteria, to
the FMC immediately.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report all incidents to the FMC immediately per IHSC incident reporting criteria.

Contractor's CQI program must include: QI committee participation, data collection/trending/planning, education needs analysis, and on-site monitoring activities (chart reviews, medication practice review, complaint investigation, corrective action monitoring, death/suicide/outbreak review, QI activity development, reevaluation, training integration, confidentiality compliance); 10 monitoring items total, list continues on page 48.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall adhere to IHSC’s Immediate Jeopardy guidelines and cooperate fully with any investigations conducted
pursuant to these guidelines.
rows.normalized: Contractor must adhere to IHSC's Immediate Jeopardy guidelines and fully cooperate with related investigations.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall promptly identify, report, and address any such situations in accordance with IHSC protocols and directives.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly identify, report, and address Immediate Jeopardy situations per IHSC protocols and directives.

rows.verbatim:
1) Access, Information, and Cooperation
The Contractor shall:
i. Provide access
a. Provide IHSC and ICE ERO/COR personnel prompt access to the facility,
relevant housing units, illegal aliens, staff, and records needed to evaluate
and address Immediate Jeopardy.
ii. Provide information and documents
a. Furnish, upon IHSC request and within the timeframes specified by
IHSC/ICE ERO, all documents and data relevant to the situation,
including medical and mental health records, detention logs, incident
reports, staffing rosters, policies, and procedures.
iii. Preserve evidence
a. Preserve relevant records and information (including, to the extent
available, video footage, electronic data, and logs) related to the
Immediate Jeopardy situation, and refrain from altering or destroying
such records except as directed by the Government.
iv. Facilitate site activities
a. Facilitate IHSC/ICE ERO ad hoc site visits, focused reviews, interviews,
and monitoring activities related to the Immediate Jeopardy finding.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide facility access, furnish requested documents/data within specified timeframes, preserve relevant records/evidence, and facilitate IHSC/ICE ERO site visits during Immediate Jeopardy investigations.

rows.verbatim:
2) Immediate Protective and Operational Measures
Upon receiving notice from IHSC/ICE ERO that Immediate Jeopardy has been identified or
is suspected, the Contractor shall, as directed by IHSC/ICE ERO:
i. Implement immediate protective measures
a. Take specified actions to protect affected illegal aliens (for example,
moving illegal aliens to safer housing, providing immediate medical or
mental health evaluation and treatment, or increasing
observation/rounding), as directed by IHSC/ICE ERO.
ii. Modify or cease unsafe practices
a. Immediately implement any operational changes ordered by IHSC/ICE
ERO that are intended to halt or mitigate the unsafe practice or condition,
which may include, but not limited to:
1. Suspending specified procedures or activities;
2. Restricting use of particular areas, equipment, or processes;
3. Adjusting staffing patterns or reassigning staff.
iii. Support transfers and population management
rows.normalized: Upon IHSC/ICE ERO notice of Immediate Jeopardy, Contractor shall implement directed protective measures, modify/cease unsafe practices as ordered, and support transfers/population management (continues on page 50).

rows.verbatim:
Cooperate with any IHSC/ICE ERO decisions regarding population caps, temporary
stops to new admissions, or transfers of illegal aliens to other facilities when these
actions are part of the Immediate Jeopardy response.
rows.normalized: Contractor must cooperate with IHSC/ICE ERO decisions on population caps, admission stops, or transfers as part of the Immediate Jeopardy response.

rows.verbatim:
3) Corrective Action Plan (UCAP) Implementation
i. Acceptance and implementation
a. Implement the Uniform Corrective Action Plan (UCAP) or other corrective
action document issued by IHSC (through the FMC/RFMC/RPM),
including all interim and long-term corrective measures specified therein.
ii. Designation of responsible staff
a. Designate facility staff responsible for carrying out each corrective action
item and for coordinating with IHSC/ICE ERO regarding progress and
obstacles.
iii. Status reporting
a. Provide IHSC/ICE ERO with updates, documentation, and data
demonstrating implementation of corrective actions in the format and
frequency specified by IHSC/ICE ERO (which may include routine written
updates and participation in follow-up calls or meetings).
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement the UCAP, designate responsible staff for corrective actions, and provide status updates to IHSC/ICE ERO in the specified format and frequency.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall not unilaterally declare Immediate Jeopardy resolved or resume any
restricted practices or operations that IHSC/ICE ERO has suspended or modified, unless
and until IHSC/ICE ERO provides written authorization.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not declare Immediate Jeopardy resolved or resume suspended/modified practices unless/until IHSC/ICE ERO provides written authorization.
Contractor must maintain complete documentation of Immediate Jeopardy response actions, including communications, interim safety measures, corrective actions, and QA monitoring results.

rows.verbatim:
b. The Contractor shall provide copies of such documentation to IHSC/ICE ERO upon
request and in the manner directed by IHSC/ICE ERO, for storage in the Government’s
designated systems.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide copies of Immediate Jeopardy documentation to IHSC/ICE ERO upon request, in the manner directed, for storage in Government systems.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall participate and respond in a timely manner or in accordance with any
applicable ICE directives or policies to the reporting requirements requested by ICE and/or IHSC.
rows.normalized: Contractor must participate and respond timely to reporting requirements requested by ICE/IHSC per applicable directives or policies.

rows.verbatim:
The following is a list of routine reporting requirements. Routinely the FMC will request any of the
following as needed or other reporting as may come up.
a. HIV
b. Hunger Strike
c. Pregnancy
d. Serious Mental Illness (SMI)/Significant Detainee Illness (SDI)
e. Suicide Watches (SW)
f. Hospital Clinical/Administrative Updates
