rows.verbatim:
Contractor shall be responsible for the following privacy and security safeguards:
a) To the extent required to carry out the FedRAMP assessment and authorization
process and FedRAMP continuous monitoring, to safeguard against threats and
hazards to the security, integrity, and confidentiality of any non-public Government
data collected and stored by the Contractor, the Contractor shall afford the
Government access to the Contractor’s facilities, installations, technical capabilities,
operations, documentation, records, and databases.
b) If new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by either the Government
or the Contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function, the discoverer
shall immediately bring the situation to the attention of the other party.
c) The contractor shall also comply with any additional FedRAMP privacy requirements.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall be responsible for privacy/security safeguards including: (a) affording the Government access to facilities, systems, and records for FedRAMP assessment and continuous monitoring; (b) immediately notifying the other party upon discovery of new/unanticipated threats or failed safeguards; (c) complying with any additional FedRAMP privacy requirements; 3 items in total.

rows.verbatim:
In accordance with the Federal Acquisitions Regulations (FAR) clause 52.239-1, contractor shall be responsible for the following
privacy and security safeguards:
i. The Contractor shall not publish or disclose in any manner, without the CO’s
written consent, the details of any safeguards either designed or developed by the
Contractor under this contract or otherwise provided by the Government.
Exception—Disclosure to a Consumer Agency for purposes of C&A verification.
ii. To the extent required to carry out a program of inspection to safeguard against
threats and hazards to the security, integrity, and confidentiality of Government
data, the Contractor shall afford the Government access to the Contractor’s
facilities, installations, technical capabilities, operations, documentation, records,
and databases within 72 hours. The program of inspection shall include, but is
not limited to: Authenticated and unauthenticated operating system/network
vulnerability scans Authenticated and unauthenticated we b application
vulnerability scans Authenticated and unauthenticated database application
vulnerability scans Automated scans can be performed by Government
personnel, or agents acting on behalf of the Government, using Government
operated equipment, and Government specified tools.
iii. If new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by either the
Government or the Contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function,
the discoverer shall immediately bring the situation to the attention of the other
party.
iv. If the vendor chooses to run its own automated scans or audits, results from these
scans may, at the Government’s discretion, be accepted in lieu of Government
performed vulnerability scans. In these cases, scanning tools and their
configuration shall be approved by the Government. In addition, the results of
vendor-conducted scans shall be provided, in full, to the Government.
rows.normalized: Per FAR 52.239-1, contractor shall follow listed safeguards: not disclose safeguard details without CO consent, provide Government facility/data access within 72 hours for inspections/scans, report new threats immediately, and if vendor runs own scans use Government-approved tools and provide full results to Government; 4 items total.

rows.verbatim: Identified gaps between required FedRAMP Security Control Baselines and Continuous Monitoring controls and the contractor's implementation as documented in the Security Assessment Report shall be tracked by the contractor for mitigation in a POA&M document.
rows.normalized: Contractor must track identified security control gaps for mitigation in a POA&M document.

rows.verbatim: The contractor is responsible for mitigating all security risks found during A&A and continuous monitoring activities.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for mitigating all security risks found during A&A and continuous monitoring.

rows.verbatim: All high-risk vulnerabilities must be mitigated within 30 days and all moderate risk vulnerabilities must be mitigated within 30 days from the date vulnerabilities are formally identified.
rows.normalized: Contractor must mitigate high- and moderate-risk vulnerabilities within 30 days of identification.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide access to the Federal Government, or their designee acting as their agent, when requested, to verify compliance with the requirements for an Information Technology security program.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide access to the Federal Government or its designee, upon request, to verify IT security program compliance.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall make appropriate personnel available for interviews and provide all necessary documentation during this review.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make personnel available for interviews and provide necessary documentation during the review.

rows.verbatim: Through continuous monitoring, security controls and supporting deliverables are updated and submitted to the FedRAMP PMO as required by FedRAMP Requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor must update and submit security controls and deliverables to the FedRAMP PMO per FedRAMP requirements.

rows.verbatim: Contractors will be required to provide updated deliverables and automated data feeds as defined in the FedRAMP Continuous Monitoring Plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide updated deliverables and automated data feeds per the FedRAMP Continuous Monitoring Plan.

rows.verbatim: All deliverables shall be labeled “Controlled Unclassified Information” (CUI).
rows.normalized: Contractor must label all deliverables as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).

rows.verbatim: External transmission/dissemination of Controlled Unclassified Information” (CUI) to or from a Government computer must be encrypted.
rows.normalized: Contractor must encrypt CUI transmitted to or from a Government computer.

rows.verbatim: Certified encryption modules must be used in accordance with FIPS PUB 140 (as amended), “Security requirements for Cryptographic Modules.”
rows.normalized: Contractor must use certified encryption modules per FIPS PUB 140.

rows.verbatim: The Cloud Service Provider vendor shall provide a system that can implement NIST SP 800-53 Control AU-10 approved controls, which provides for origin authentication, data integrity, and signer non-repudiation.
rows.normalized: Vendor must provide a system implementing NIST SP 800-53 AU-10 non-repudiation controls.

rows.verbatim: The vendor shall support a secure, multi-factor method of remote authentication and authorization to identified Government Administrators that will allow Government designated personnel the ability to perform management duties on the system.
rows.normalized: Vendor must support secure multi-factor remote authentication for Government Administrators.

rows.verbatim: The vendor shall support multi-factor authentication including User ID and Password, digital certificate, PIV or smart card, PIN.
rows.normalized: Vendor must support multi-factor authentication including User ID/Password, digital certificate, PIV/smart card, and PIN.

rows.verbatim: The vendor shall support a secure, dual factor method of remote authentication and authorization to identified Vendor Administrators that will allow vendor-designated personnel the ability to perform management duties on the system.
rows.normalized: Vendor must support secure dual-factor remote authentication for Vendor Administrators.

rows.verbatim: Cloud Service Providers are required to report all computer security incidents to the United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (U.S.-CERT) in accordance with U.S.-CERT “Incident Categories and Reporting Timeframes” in , Appendix J, Table J-1 of NIST SP 800-61 (as amended), “Computer Security Incident Handling Guide.”
rows.normalized: CSP must report all computer security incidents to U.S.-CERT per NIST SP 800-61 timeframes.

rows.verbatim:
Any
Category (CAT) 1, CAT 2, or CAT 3 incident, must be reported immediately to their Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) and the Senior Agency Information Security Officer (SAISO).
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately report CAT 1, 2, or 3 incidents to the ISSO and SAISO.

rows.verbatim: Any incident that involves compromised Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must be reported to U.S.-CERT within 1 hour of detection regardless of the incident category reporting timeframe.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any PII-compromising incident to U.S.-CERT within 1 hour of detection.

rows.verbatim: The vendor shall document activities associated with the transport of Federal agency information stored on digital and non-digital media and employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of this information during transport outside of controlled areas.
rows.normalized: Vendor must document media-transport activities and use cryptographic protection during transport outside controlled areas.

rows.verbatim: Digital media, containing Federal agency information, that is transported outside of controlled areas must be encrypted using AES 256; non-digital media including but not limited to CD-ROM, floppy disks, etc., must be secured using the same policies and procedures as paper.
rows.normalized: Digital media transported outside controlled areas must be AES 256 encrypted; non-digital media must be secured per paper procedures.

rows.verbatim: Media, containing Federal Agency information that is transported outside of controlled areas must ensure accountability.
rows.normalized: Transported media containing Federal Agency information must ensure accountability.

rows.verbatim: Federal Agency data that resides on mobile/portable devices (e.g., USB flash drives, external hard 12 drives, and SD cards) must be encrypted using AES 256.
rows.normalized: Federal Agency data on mobile/portable devices must be encrypted with AES 256.

rows.verbatim: All Federal Agency data residing on laptop computing devices must be protected with approved encryption software.
rows.normalized: Federal Agency data on laptops must be protected with approved encryption software.

rows.verbatim: The CSP/Reseller shall route all external connections through a Trusted Internet Connection (TIC).
rows.normalized: CSP/Reseller must route all external connections through a TIC.

rows.verbatim: The CSP shall provide security mechanisms for handling data at rest and in transit in accordance with FIPS 140-2.
rows.normalized: CSP must provide FIPS 140-2 compliant security mechanisms for data at rest and in transit.

rows.verbatim: The CSP/Reseller shall provide a list of their personnel, identified by name and role, with system 1 administration, monitoring, and/or security responsibilities that are to receive security alerts, two advisories, and directives.
rows.normalized: CSP/Reseller must provide a list of personnel (by name/role) who receive security alerts, advisories, and directives.

rows.verbatim: This list shall include ICE SOC.
rows.normalized: The personnel list must include ICE SOC.

rows.verbatim:
If encryption is required, the following methods are acceptable for encrypting sensitive information:
a) FIPS 197 (Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)) 256 algorithm and cryptographic modules that have been validated under FIPS 140-2.
b) National Security Agency (NSA) Type 2 or Type 1 encryption.
c) Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) (see paragraph 5.5.2.1 of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) IT Security Program Handbook (DHS Management Directive (MD)
4300A) for Sensitive Systems).
rows.normalized: If encryption is required, contractor must use one of the acceptable methods: FIPS 197 AES 256, NSA Type 1/2 encryption, or PKI per DHS MD 4300A.

rows.verbatim: Interconnections between DHS and non-DHS IT systems shall be established only through controlled interfaces and via approved contractors.
rows.normalized: Interconnections between DHS and non-DHS systems must be established only through controlled interfaces and approved contractors.

rows.verbatim: The controlled interfaces shall be authorized at the highest security level of information on the network.
rows.normalized: Controlled interfaces must be authorized at the network's highest security level.

rows.verbatim: Connections with other Federal agencies shall be documented based on interagency agreements; memoranda of understanding, service level agreements or interconnection security agreements.
rows.normalized: Connections with other Federal agencies must be documented via interagency agreements, MOUs, SLAs, or ISAs.

rows.verbatim: Procurements for products, systems, services, hardware, or software involving controlled federal facility or information system shall be PIV-enabled by accepting HSPD-12 PIV credentials as a method of identity verification and authentication.
rows.normalized: Procurements involving controlled facilities/systems must be PIV-enabled accepting HSPD-12 credentials.

rows.verbatim: Procurements for software products or software developments shall be compliant by accepting PIV credentials as the common means of authentication for access for federal employees and contractors.
rows.normalized: Software procurements/developments must accept PIV credentials as the common authentication means.

rows.verbatim: PIV-enabled information systems must demonstrate that they can correctly work with PIV credentials by responding to the cryptographic challenge in the authentication protocol before granting access.
rows.normalized: PIV-enabled systems must correctly respond to cryptographic challenge before granting access.

rows.verbatim: If a system is identified to be non-compliant with HSPD-12 for PIV credential enablement, a remediation plan for achieving HSPD-12 compliance shall be required for review, evaluation, and approval by the CISO.
rows.normalized: If a system is non-compliant with HSPD-12, contractor must submit a remediation plan for CISO review/approval.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall perform patch management services.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform patch management services.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall push patches that are required by vendors and DHS system owner.
rows.normalized: Contractor must push patches required by vendors and the DHS system owner.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall be informed by DHS which patches are required by DHS through the Information Security Vulnerability Management bulletins and advisories.
rows.normalized: DHS will inform the contractor of required patches via Information Security Vulnerability Management bulletins/advisories.

rows.verbatim: However, the contractor shall be responsible for deploying patches as directed by DHS.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for deploying patches as directed by DHS.

rows.verbatim: It is recommended that all other applications (host-based intrusion detection system (HIDS), network intrusion detection system (NIDS), Anti-malware, and Firewall) shall be tested by the contractor prior to deployment in a test environment.
rows.normalized: Contractor should/shall test other applications (HIDS, NIDS, Anti-malware, Firewall) prior to deployment.

rows.verbatim: The contractor is responsible for identifying detainees with limited English proficiency (i.e., who do not speak English as their primary language and who have limited ability to read, speak, write, or understand English) and providing them access to all facility programs and services through language assistance (accurate, timely, and effective communication) at no cost to the detainee.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for identifying LEP detainees and providing free language assistance for access to programs/services.

rows.verbatim: If the contractor uses Wi-Fi connected technology, then the safety, security, and/or privacy risks will be assessed if any personally identifiable or other sensitive information is stored or shared.
rows.normalized: If contractor uses Wi-Fi connected technology, risks must be assessed when PII or sensitive information is stored/shared.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall secure and utilize its own contract for professional language services.
rows.normalized: Contractor must secure and use its own contract for professional language services.

rows.verbatim: All facility postings and written materials provided to aliens shall generally be translated via professional language services into Spanish and other languages spoken by significant segments of the detained ICE population with limited English proficiency at the facility.
rows.normalized: Facility postings and written materials must generally be translated into Spanish and other significant LEP languages via professional services.

rows.verbatim: Other than in emergencies, and even then, only until appropriate language services can be procured, other aliens shall not be used for interpretation or translation services.
rows.normalized: Other aliens shall not be used for interpretation/translation except briefly during emergencies until proper services are procured.

rows.verbatim: In such situations, the contractor must notify the COR within 24 hours of the emergency.
rows.normalized: In emergency interpretation situations, contractor must notify the COR within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: The contractor must have their own sign language or certified deaf interpretation service.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have its own sign language or certified deaf interpretation service.

rows.verbatim: The contractor will provide auxiliary aids and services to detainees with communication impairments to ensure there is effective communication between the detainee and facility staff, and detainees and outside stakeholders, such as consulates, attorneys, and religious services providers.
rows.normalized: Contractor will provide auxiliary aids and services to detainees with communication impairments to ensure effective communication.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor must have at minimum the following auxiliary assistive devices at the facility:
1. Sound Amplifier
2. Magnifying Glasses or similar
3. Audio Reader technology
4. Varying types of batteries for hearing aids
5. Varying non-prescription strength eyeglasses
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain at minimum 5 listed auxiliary assistive devices at the facility.

rows.verbatim: The multi-purpose spaces for religious services shall accommodate multiple religious services per week accommodating multiple faith groups sufficient to meet the needs of all aliens who want to participate and considering different classification levels and sexes.
rows.normalized: Multi-purpose religious service spaces shall accommodate multiple religious services per week for multiple faith groups, considering classification levels and sexes.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide programming for detainees, including religious services and social programs.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide programming for detainees, including religious services and social programs.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide a dedicated Chaplain or religious service coordinator to provide all religious activities consistent with the requirements of the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a dedicated Chaplain or religious service coordinator for all religious activities consistent with ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall provide dedicated space for religious services.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide dedicated space for religious services.

rows.verbatim: The design and operation of this space shall be consistent with the requirements of the most recent version of the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: Design and operation of the contractor-provided religious space shall be consistent with the most recent applicable ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim: The contractor must maintain a stock of frequently requested religious worship or prayer items, such as religious scriptures/text of various faiths in various languages, rosaries, saint cards, prayer rugs, religious headwear, statues, etc.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain a stock of frequently requested religious worship/prayer items across various faiths.

rows.verbatim:
If requested religious items are needed and not available within the facility, the contractor
must facilitate the procurement of the items through in-kind donations from family/friends,
religious community, or other non-governmental organization, or by purchasing the items.
rows.normalized: If requested religious items are needed and unavailable at the facility, contractor must facilitate procurement via donations or purchase.

rows.verbatim: The detention facility shall provide dedicated space for religious services.
rows.normalized: Facility shall provide dedicated space for religious services.

rows.verbatim: One multiple purpose space for religious services is not sufficient.
rows.normalized: A single multi-purpose religious space is deemed insufficient; more than one is required.

rows.verbatim: The facility will provide one indoor multiple purpose area per 500 beds.
rows.normalized: Facility will provide one indoor multi-purpose area per 500 beds.

rows.verbatim: Donated or purchased items to the facility may be retained by the facility upon a detainee’s release or removal, if maintaining the items is not a sanitation concern (e.g. headwear worn by detainees should not be maintained).
rows.normalized: Facility may retain donated/purchased items after a detainee's release or removal only if not a sanitation concern.

rows.verbatim:
Donated items designated for a specific detainee at
the time of the donation, shall become the personal property of the detainee, and may not be retained by the facility.
rows.normalized: Donated items designated for a specific detainee become the detainee's personal property and facility may not retain them.

rows.verbatim:
The facility shall provide private areas for in-person
attorney-client visits equipped with phones, as well as spaces with video teleconferencing
capabilities (in-person spaces can include video teleconferencing capabilities or the facility
can opt for Virtual Attorney Visitation rooms/booths for video teleconferencing).
rows.normalized: Facility must provide private attorney-client visit spaces with phones and video teleconferencing capability.

rows.verbatim:
The detention facility shall provide space(s) for a law library that includes connectivity
sufficient to allow computers with limited web access to load the ICE provided online law
library via the ICE Portal (including websites referenced therein).
rows.normalized: Facility must provide law library space(s) with connectivity for the ICE online law library.

rows.verbatim:
The number of law library spaces
shall be sufficient to accommodate each sex and classification level for a minimum
of five (5) hours a week.
rows.normalized: Law library spaces must accommodate each sex/classification level for a minimum of 5 hours weekly.

rows.verbatim:
The facility shall provide easy access to legal services and
meet all requirements of the most recent version of the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: Facility must provide easy legal-services access and meet current ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim:
The facility shall provide law library coordinator staff with
requisite training and/or certification in the following areas to support detained aliens use of
the library:
o Legal research materials and tools, including electronic law library media provided by
ICE
o Notary certification to provide free, notary services as needed language services
(including use of language line).
rows.normalized: Facility must provide trained/certified law library coordinator staff covering listed areas; 2 items listed.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor will provide a multi-purpose space that can accommodate group legal orientation
presentations.
rows.normalized: Contractor will provide a multi-purpose space for group legal orientation presentations.

rows.verbatim: The space shall accommodate no less than 40 aliens and include tables and chairs.
rows.normalized: The orientation space must accommodate no less than 40 aliens with tables and chairs.

rows.verbatim:
The space shall also be equipped with speakers and/or headsets, audio-visual equipment for
presentations, and video-conferencing capability for virtual presentations.
rows.normalized: The orientation space must be equipped with speakers/headsets, AV equipment, and video-conferencing capability.

rows.verbatim:
The multi-purpose
space shall be made available for legal presentations for no less than two presentations for three
hours in length (including group and individual orientations), three times a week (Monday
through Friday).
rows.normalized: The multi-purpose space must be available for no less than two 3-hour legal presentations, three times weekly (Monday-Friday).

rows.verbatim:
The ICE designated Alien Communication Services Contractor shall be the exclusive provider
of alien communications (phones, tablets) for this federal facility.
rows.normalized: The ICE-designated Alien Communication Services Contractor must be the exclusive provider of alien communications for the facility.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be
allowed to install vending debit machines and shall receive 100 percent of all revenue collected
by sales of prepaid debit services.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be allowed to install vending debit machines and shall receive 100 percent of prepaid debit service revenue.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be responsible for the costs incurred for
installation of the equipment, any monthly telephone charges incurred from the operation of an
alien telephone system, and the maintenance and operation of the system.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for installation costs, monthly telephone charges, and system maintenance/operation.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall
not be entitled to any commissions, fees, or revenues generated using the alien telephone system or the alien telephones.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not be entitled to any commissions, fees, or revenues from the alien telephone system.

rows.verbatim: If authorized to do so under applicable law, the Contractor shall monitor and record alien conversations.
rows.normalized: If authorized under applicable law, Contractor shall monitor and record alien conversations.

rows.verbatim: If alien telephone conversations can be monitored under applicable law, the Contractor shall provide notice to aliens of the potential for monitoring.
rows.normalized: If conversations can be monitored under law, Contractor shall notify aliens of potential monitoring.

rows.verbatim: However, the Contractor shall also provide procedures at the federal facility for aliens to be able to place unmonitored telephone calls to their attorneys.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide procedures for aliens to place unmonitored calls to attorneys.

rows.verbatim: Telephone rates will not exceed the Federal Communications Commission rates for inmate telephone service, as well as established state rates where applicable, and shall conform to all applicable federal, state, and local telephone regulations.
rows.normalized: Telephone rates will not exceed FCC/state rates and shall conform to applicable telephone regulations.

rows.verbatim: The facility shall provide indoor and outdoor space for recreational activities appropriate for the detainee population and consistent with the requirements of the most recent version of the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: The facility (contractor) shall provide indoor and outdoor recreational space consistent with ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim: The facility shall provide detainees with access to recreational programs and activities, held outdoors when available, within the constraints of the safety and security of the facility and consistent with the requirements under the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: The facility shall provide detainees access to recreational programs and activities, outdoors when available, consistent with ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim: No more than 250 aliens shall be in one recreational space at any one time.
rows.normalized: The facility shall limit occupancy of any one recreational space to no more than 250 aliens at a time.

rows.verbatim: Recreation shall be offered at a reasonable time of day.
rows.normalized: The facility shall offer recreation at a reasonable time of day.

rows.verbatim: Weather permitting, each detainee shall have access for at least one hour per day, five days per week; or, six or more hours per week, at least four days per week that allows for vigorous aerobic exercise with extended hours of availability.
rows.normalized: The facility shall ensure each detainee has recreation access of at least one hour/day five days/week, or six+ hours/week over at least four days, weather permitting.

rows.verbatim: Detainees shall not be required to work, except for personal housekeeping.
rows.normalized: The facility shall not require detainees to work, except for personal housekeeping.

rows.verbatim: Detainee volunteers shall not be used as substitutes for facility employees or assigned work in areas where sensitive documents are stored, such as designated ICE workspaces.
rows.normalized: The facility shall not use detainee volunteers as substitutes for facility employees or in areas storing sensitive documents.

rows.verbatim: The facility shall provide sufficient security staff to supervise detainees participating in the voluntary work program.
rows.normalized: The facility shall provide sufficient security staff to supervise detainees in the voluntary work program.

rows.verbatim: Work assignments must remain within the security perimeter unless approved by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR).
rows.normalized: Work assignments must stay within the security perimeter unless the COR approves an exception.

rows.verbatim: High-custody detainees shall not, under any circumstances, work outside the secure outer perimeter.
rows.normalized: The facility shall not allow high-custody detainees to work outside the secure outer perimeter under any circumstances.

rows.verbatim: If the facility has a voluntary work program, the facility shall develop a voluntary work program plan, subject to approval by the COR.
rows.normalized: If the facility operates a voluntary work program, the facility shall develop a program plan subject to COR approval.

rows.verbatim: All detainees shall be searched when they are returned from work details.
rows.normalized: Facility shall search all detainees when returned from work details.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility shall develop site-specific rules for selecting work detail volunteers
rows.normalized: Facility shall develop site-specific rules for selecting work detail volunteers.

rows.verbatim: Detainees shall not be denied voluntary work opportunities based solely on race, religion, national origin, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, or disability.
rows.normalized: Facility shall not deny voluntary work opportunities based on protected characteristics.

rows.verbatim: Where possible, the federal facility shall allow detainees with disabilities to participate in the voluntary work program through appropriate work assignments.
rows.normalized: Where possible, facility shall allow detainees with disabilities to participate via appropriate assignments.

rows.verbatim: Detainees participating in the voluntary work program shall adhere to a fixed schedule, working no more than 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week.
rows.normalized: Voluntary work program detainees shall work no more than 8 hrs/day and 40 hrs/week on a fixed schedule.

rows.verbatim: Detainees shall not receive a stipend exceeding the amount Congressionally allocated to ICE for reimbursing contract facilities in support of the Voluntary Work Program.
rows.normalized: Facility shall not pay detainee stipends exceeding the Congressionally allocated amount.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility is responsible for ensuring detainees receive their owed reimbursement in cash (USD) before transfer or release.
rows.normalized: Facility is responsible for ensuring detainees receive owed reimbursement in cash before transfer or release.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility shall document the justification for removal in the detainee’s detention file or a retrievable electronic record.
rows.normalized: Facility shall document justification for removal from work detail in detainee's file or electronic record.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility shall establish procedures to inform detainee volunteers of their job responsibilities and reporting procedures.
rows.normalized: Facility shall establish procedures to inform detainee volunteers of job responsibilities and reporting procedures.

rows.verbatim: Detainees must use safety equipment and follow other precautions as instructed by the work supervisor.
rows.normalized: Detainees must use safety equipment and follow precautions as instructed by the work supervisor.

rows.verbatim:
Detention facilities shall comply with all applicable federal health and safety
regulations and standards.
rows.normalized: The detention facility must comply with all applicable federal health and safety regulations and standards.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim: Detainees shall be provided basic OSHA protections and appropriate safety/protective clothing and equipment during work assignments.
rows.normalized: The facility must provide detainees basic OSHA protections and appropriate safety/protective clothing and equipment during work assignments.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
Medical staff shall ensure detainees are medically screened and certified before
undertaking food service assignments.
rows.normalized: Medical staff must ensure detainees are medically screened and certified before food service assignments.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
The federal facility shall ensure all
department heads develop appropriate training for detainee workers.
rows.normalized: The facility must ensure all department heads develop appropriate training for detainee workers.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
Before beginning any job or work detail, the supervisor shall provide the
detainee with thorough instructions on safe work methods and, if applicable, hazardous materials.
rows.normalized: Before any job or work detail, the supervisor must provide the detainee thorough instructions on safe work methods and hazardous materials if applicable.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
The detainee must sign a voluntary work program agreement,
confirming they have received and understood the training provided by the
supervisor.
rows.normalized: The detainee must sign a voluntary work program agreement confirming receipt/understanding of training.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
The agreement shall be placed in the detainee’s detention file or
retrievable electronic record.
rows.normalized: The signed work agreement must be placed in the detainee's detention file or retrievable electronic record.
rows.section_ref: SOW g. Detainee Training and Safety

rows.verbatim:
The federal facility shall establish procedures to immediately and appropriately respond
to on-the-job injuries, including immediate notification to ICE/ERO.
rows.normalized: The facility must establish procedures to immediately and appropriately respond to on-the-job injuries, including immediate notification to ICE/ERO.
rows.section_ref: SOW h. Detainee Injury and Reporting Procedures

rows.verbatim:
The Case Processing Specialist shall hold an accredited associate or bachelor’s degree in an
appropriate discipline or have a minimum of one year of directly related industry experience.
rows.normalized: The Case Processing Specialist must hold an accredited associate or bachelor's degree or have at least one year of directly related industry experience.
rows.section_ref: SOW 49. Detention Facility ERO Case Processing Specialists Position Description

rows.verbatim:
The
Case Processing Specialist will have knowledge of program objectives, policies, procedures, and
requirements related to immigration case processing.
rows.normalized: The Case Processing Specialist must have knowledge of program objectives, policies, procedures, and requirements related to immigration case processing.
rows.section_ref: SOW 49. Detention Facility ERO Case Processing Specialists Position Description

rows.verbatim:
The Case Processing Specialist must have
prior experience and/or training related to reviewing law enforcement documentation such detention
files, custodial records, or immigration case files including A-files and DHS databases, or previous
experience conducting interviews for immigration or detention related purposes.
rows.normalized: The Case Processing Specialist must have prior experience/training in reviewing law enforcement documentation or immigration case files, or prior interview experience for immigration/detention purposes.
rows.section_ref: SOW 49. Detention Facility ERO Case Processing Specialists Position Description

rows.verbatim:
Case Processing Specialists shall assist ICE Personnel with the following duties under the general
direction of ICE field office personnel:
1. Case Processing, Docket Management, Data Entry and Records Management duties:
a. Process cases and perform all peripheral activities, immigration records management, and
document preparation.
b. Prepare, review, and manage case files, ensuring accuracy and completeness in all
documentation.
c. Ensure Alien Files (A-files) and ICE systems reflect a case status that is updated, accurate, and
complete.
d. Accurately enter data into ICE systems, ensuring compliance with agency protocols and data
integrity requirements.
rows.normalized: Case Processing Specialists must assist ICE Personnel with listed case processing, docket management, data entry, and records management duties (items a-d shown; list continues beyond excerpt).
rows.section_ref: SOW 49. Detention Facility ERO Case Processing Specialists Position Description

rows.verbatim:
Once completed, the DTT must be submitted via e-
mail to both the ERO Field Office COR and the ERO RPA Team Mailbox.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the completed DTT via email to the ERO Field Office COR and the ERO RPA Team Mailbox.

rows.verbatim:
There shall be no public disclosure regarding this contract made by the Contractor (or any
subcontractors) without review and approval of such disclosure by ICE Public Affairs.
rows.normalized: Contractor (and subcontractors) shall not publicly disclose information about the contract without prior review and approval by ICE Public Affairs.

rows.verbatim:
All records related to contract performance shall be retained in a retrievable format for the duration
of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall retain all contract-performance records in a retrievable format for the duration of the contract.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall, upon completion or termination of the contract, transmit to the
government any records related to the performance of the contract, in a format acceptable to the
CO.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transmit all performance-related records to the government upon completion or termination of the contract, in a format acceptable to the CO.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall comply with all statutes, regulations, and guidelines from the National
Archives and Records Administration (NARA).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall comply with all NARA statutes, regulations, and guidelines.

rows.verbatim:
Policies and procedures shall be developed to ensure the confidentiality and security of all
alien files.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall develop policies and procedures to ensure the confidentiality and security of all alien files.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be responsible for alien record keeping services and personal property.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for alien record keeping services and personal property.

rows.verbatim:
The Detention Facility Robotics Process Automation (RPA) process requires that data supporting
detention bed space, ground transportation, and any other additional costs covered by the current
contract will be recorded utilizing the Detention Transportation Template (DTT) (see attachment).
rows.normalized: The contractor must record data supporting detention bed space, ground transportation, and other additional contract costs using the Detention Transportation Template (DTT).

rows.verbatim:
This data template should be completed in its entirety in the established format once all data
supporting the monthly operations is available.
rows.normalized: The contractor should complete the DTT in its entirety in the established format once monthly operations data is available.

rows.verbatim:
Please note that the requirement for submission of the DTT is prior to and in addition to the invoice submission
requirement already included in this contract.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to the officer’s initial assignment or reassignment to the federal facility, the Contractor shall certify in writing to the COR that each detention officer is in
full compliance with the following:
a. Staff shall not have diseases that may be transmitted to and result in the disablement of
other individuals and shall be physically and mentally able to perform the essential
functions of their position, either with or without reasonable accommodation, and
without creating a significant risk of substantial harm to the health or safety of that officer
or others, which risk cannot be eliminated or reduced by a reasonable accommodation.
b. Detention officers are required to have the following:
c. Correctable distant vision must be equal to or better than 20/20 in each eye.
d. Binocular distant vision must be correctable to 20/20.
e. Monocular vision is generally disqualifying; depth perception must be equal to or better than 70 seconds of arc.
f. Peripheral vision must be normal.
g. Color vision must be normal.
i. Acceptable measure of color discrimination is the Ishihara color (14 plates). X
chrome lenses are not acceptable to ICE as a means of correcting color
deficiencies. Any disease or condition which interferes with a person’s vision
may be considered disqualifying. Cases will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis
by the COR.
h. Detention officers are required to be able to hear in the frequency range from 500-2000
hertz (Hz), the deficit should not exceed 30 decibels in either ear. At 3000 Hz, the deficit
should not exceed 40 decibels in either ear. Any disease or condition, which interferes
with the ability to hear, may be considered disqualifying. Cases will be reviewed on a
case-by-case basis by the COR.
i. Detention officers shall not have heart, lung, skeletal, or other physical defects that
would impair their ability to perform effectively in either normal or emergency
situations.
j. Detention officers shall possess unimpaired use of hands, arms, legs, and feet.
k. detention officers shall be able to run when necessary and be capable of handling
portable fire extinguishers, building fire hoses, and related equipment.
l. Detention officers shall be able to wear all necessary equipment, or other protective
items.
m. Officers shall be mentally alert and emotionally stable with an absence of detectable
neurotic or psychoneurotic conditions that would affect their ability to act during a
stressful situation involving mental stress.
n. As required by the OSHA, 29 CFR, Part 1910.1035 (Occupational Exposure to
Tuberculosis), all employees in occupations with high-risk exposure are required to have
a TB Skin Test completed annually. The Contractor shall complete a baseline test on all
newly hired employees. Each employee must have a TB Skin Test Certificate prior to
entering on his/her first day of duty. The Contractor shall be responsible for re-testing
employees annually.
