rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct admissions screening, file review, body search, and personal belongings inventory for aliens.

rows.verbatim: This includes fingerprinting of aliens.
rows.normalized: Admissions process includes fingerprinting of aliens.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure aliens are classified appropriately using objective criteria.
rows.normalized: Contractor must classify aliens appropriately using objective criteria.

rows.verbatim: Aliens will be classified upon arrival, before being admitted to the general population.
rows.normalized: Aliens must be classified upon arrival before general population admission.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will periodically re-classify aliens, in accordance with the applicable ICE detention standards.
rows.normalized: Contractor must periodically re-classify aliens per ICE detention standards.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall effectuate departures.
rows.normalized: Contractor must effectuate alien departures.

rows.verbatim: Effectuating departures require Contractor employees to perform alien-related activities including but not limited to positive identification, documentation preparation and review, provision of any sack lunches required, transportation, escorting and returning all DHS documentation to the appropriate ICE supervisor upon completing the escort assignment.
rows.normalized: Contractor employees must perform listed departure-related activities (identification, documentation, sack lunches, transportation, escorting, returning DHS documentation), at least 6 items in total.

rows.verbatim: In addition, Contractor employees shall, when required by proper authority, affirm, swear, and witness to all actions of effectuating departure that were accomplished, performed, carried out, and done, and in transactions involving the alien(s), when required in a legal setting, deposition, or court of law.
rows.normalized: If required by proper authority, Contractor employees must affirm/swear/witness departure actions in legal settings.

rows.verbatim: Aliens that are released should, prior to release, be given the opportunity to make a free phone call to arrange for pick up from the federal facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor should give released aliens the opportunity to make a free phone call prior to release.

rows.verbatim: Aliens that are released shall be transported to a local airport, bus terminal, train station, or subway station prior to the time of the last departure at their destination, so the released individual would depart the same day, and not be required to spend time overnight in a transportation terminal.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transport released aliens to transportation hubs in time for same-day departure.

rows.verbatim: The time, point, and manner of release from a federal facility shall be consistent with safety considerations and consider special vulnerabilities.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure release time/point/manner considers safety and vulnerabilities.

rows.verbatim: If public transportation is within walking distance of the federal facility, aliens shall be provided with an information sheet that gives directions to and describes the types of transportation services available.
rows.normalized: If public transportation is within walking distance, Contractor must provide aliens an information sheet on transportation options.

rows.verbatim: However, the federal facility must provide transportation for any alien who is not reasonably able to walk due to age, disability, illness, mental health, or other vulnerability.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for aliens unable to walk due to vulnerability.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the federal facility must provide transportation for any alien because of weather or other environmental conditions at the time of release that may endanger the safety of the alien.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for aliens when weather/environmental conditions endanger safety.

rows.verbatim: If an alien resided in the local area near the federal facility prior to arrest and is released to the same local area upon release, they shall be provided with a list of shelter services available, along with directions to each shelter.
rows.normalized: If alien is released to local area of prior residence, Contractor must provide list of shelter services and directions.

rows.verbatim: As practicable, aliens shall be provided with a laundered set of their own clothing, or one set of non-institutional clothing and footwear that is weather-appropriate for their destination.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide aliens laundered or non-institutional clothing/footwear appropriate to destination weather.

rows.verbatim: A commissary shall be operated by the Contractor as a privilege to aliens who will have the opportunity to purchase from the commissary at least once per week.
rows.normalized: Contractor must operate a commissary allowing aliens to purchase at least once per week.

rows.verbatim: All items available at the commissary must be approved by the COR and ICE officials.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have all commissary items approved by COR and ICE officials.

rows.verbatim: The commissary inventory shall be provided to the COR upon request.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide commissary inventory to COR upon request.

rows.verbatim: Notice of any price increases must be provided to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify COR of price increases.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor may assess sales tax on the price of items if state sales tax is applicable.
rows.normalized: Contractor may assess sales tax on commissary items only if state sales tax applies.

rows.verbatim: Revenues shall be maintained in the federal facility commissary account and not commingled with any other funds.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep commissary revenues in dedicated account, not commingled.

rows.verbatim: If funds are placed in an interest-bearing account, the interest earned shall be credited to the aliens.
rows.normalized: If commissary funds are interest-bearing, interest earned must be credited to aliens.

rows.verbatim: Any expenditure of funds from the account shall only be made with the approval of the CO.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain CO approval before expending commissary account funds.

rows.verbatim: Any revenues earned more than what is required for commissary operations shall be used solely to benefit aliens at the federal facility.
rows.normalized: Excess commissary revenues must be used solely to benefit aliens.

rows.verbatim: Using these funds for any expense for which the Contractor is required to pay is prohibited.
rows.normalized: Contractor is prohibited from using commissary funds for its own required expenses.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide independent auditor certification of the funds to the COR every 90 days.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide independent auditor certification of commissary funds to COR every 90 days.

rows.verbatim: At the end of the contract period, or as directed by the CO, a check for any profits remaining in this account associated with alien commissary purchases shall be made payable to the Treasury general trust fund.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make remaining commissary profits payable to Treasury general trust fund at contract end or as directed.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall coordinate with the COR to return funds as required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must coordinate with COR to return commissary funds as required.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for all alien personal property (i.e., stolen/misplaced goods due to Contractor negligence and/or mishandling of alien personal property).
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for alien personal property including losses due to negligence/mishandling.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have written policies and procedures in managing personal property.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have written policies for managing personal property.

rows.verbatim: The safeguarding of personal property will include: the secure storage and return of funds, valuables, baggage, and other personal property; a procedure for documentation and receipting of surrendered property; and the initial and regularly scheduled inventories of all funds, valuables, and other property.
rows.normalized: Contractor's safeguarding of personal property must include the three listed elements (secure storage/return, documentation procedure, scheduled inventories).

rows.verbatim: Written procedures shall be established for returning funds, valuables, and personal property to an alien being transferred or released that adheres to the requirements of ICE policy.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish written procedures for returning property to transferred/released aliens per ICE policy.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that all aliens who are scheduled for either transfer or release are given all funds (in cash or check, whichever is deemed appropriate by the COR or designated ICE official) immediately prior to leaving the federal facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure aliens receive all funds immediately prior to transfer/release.

rows.verbatim: Confiscated foreign currency funds are to be returned to the alien.
rows.normalized: Contractor must return confiscated foreign currency funds to the alien.

rows.verbatim: For such removal flights, the Contractor will provide all necessary items for removal processing.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide all necessary items for removal processing on removal flights.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall return or discard any unclaimed, undesired, or abandoned property to the last known address of the alien or his designated contact.
rows.normalized: Contractor must return or discard unclaimed/abandoned property to alien's last known address.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall log all property returned or discarded, the address where the property was sent, and the date the property was shipped or destroyed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must log all returned/discarded property with address and date.

rows.verbatim: Property shall be checked at least once per month to ensure that there is not an excess of property left in the federal facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must check property at least once per month for excess.

rows.verbatim: Staff responsible for lock maintenance shall receive training and be certified from a government approved training program specializing in the operation of locks and locking mechanisms.
rows.normalized: Contractor lock-maintenance staff must receive training and certification from a government-approved program.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide constant less than lethal armed perimeter surveillance of the federal facility.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide constant less-than-lethal armed perimeter surveillance.

rows.verbatim: The facility shall have sufficient auxiliary power for emergency/security systems through generator or battery back-up to maintain secure operations, consistent with necessary environmental permitting and the Clean Air Act.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide sufficient auxiliary power for emergency/security systems.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall develop and implement a comprehensive sexual abuse/assault prevention and intervention program in accordance with Standard 2.11, Sexual Abuse and Assault Prevention and Intervention, found in the applicable ICE detention standards, and all federal facility requirements of the DHS PREA (Standards to Prevent, Detect, and Respond to Sexual Abuse and Assault in Confinement Facilities, 79 Fed. Reg. 13100 (Mar. 7, 2014)), as outlined in Attachment – Prison Rape Elimination Act Regulations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must develop and implement a PREA-compliant sexual abuse/assault prevention program per Standard 2.11.

rows.verbatim: This program shall include training and/or information that is given separately to both staff and aliens.
rows.normalized: PREA program must include separate training/information for staff and aliens.

rows.verbatim: Visitation and/or tours of the federal facility shall be conducted in accordance with the relevant provisions of the applicable ICE detention standards or as directed by ICE.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct visitation/tours per ICE detention standards or as directed.

rows.verbatim: For the safety and privacy of the aliens, no videotaping or audio recording devices are permitted by visitors or others (including Contractor employees) within the secure perimeter without prior approval from ICE.
rows.normalized: Contractor employees may not use videotaping/audio recording devices within secure perimeter without prior ICE approval.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall comply with all federal security and privacy laws and regulations established to protect federal systems and data.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with federal security/privacy laws protecting federal systems and data.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall inform all personnel of the confidential nature of ICE alien information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inform personnel of the confidentiality of ICE alien information.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall restrict access to data information pertaining to ICE aliens to authorized employees with the appropriate clearance who require this information in the course of their official duties.
rows.normalized: Contractor must restrict access to ICE alien data to authorized, cleared employees with need.

rows.verbatim: In accordance with the Freedom of Information/Privacy Act, the contractor shall not disclose information obtained pertaining to ICE detainees to a third party without written permission from the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not disclose ICE detainee information to third parties without COR written permission.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor may not disclose information pertaining to ICE aliens to a third party without written permission from the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor may not disclose ICE alien information to third parties without COR written permission.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall develop a procedural system to identify and record unauthorized access or attempts to access ICE alien information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must develop a system to identify/record unauthorized access attempts to ICE alien information.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall notify the COR and ICE officials within four hours of a security incident.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify COR and ICE officials within four hours of a security incident.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility shall include at least one non-segregated (i.e., not a segregation housing unit) protective custody housing option for placing aliens who may benefit from a more supportive or specialized general population setting together by biological sex.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide at least one non-segregated protective custody housing option by biological sex.

rows.verbatim: The number of non-segregated protective custody housing options should appropriately reflect the federal facility population, and at a minimum, include both male and female housing options (if the federal facility houses female population).
rows.normalized: Contractor must, at a minimum, provide both male and female non-segregated protective custody housing options if applicable.

rows.verbatim: Non-segregated protective custody housing units shall be staffed by federal facility personnel who should be trained in working with vulnerable populations and trauma-informed care.
rows.normalized: Contractor must staff non-segregated protective custody housing with trained personnel.

rows.verbatim: Aliens in non-segregated protective custody housing will have equal access to all federal facility services and programming available to aliens in general population housing and shall not include any limitations not applied to the general population.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide equal access to services/programming for protective custody housing without additional limitations.

rows.verbatim: Additional programming applicable to the population in non-segregated protective custody housing units shall be offered.
rows.normalized: Contractor must offer additional applicable programming for non-segregated protective custody housing.

rows.verbatim: Non-segregated protective custody housing units shall include self-help materials and pro-social organized activities, including those which will assist with promoting a calm environment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include self-help materials and pro-social activities in protective custody housing.

rows.verbatim: The federal facility shall maintain a multi-disciplinary team to oversee and manage placement in non-segregated protective custody housing units.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain a multi-disciplinary team to manage protective custody housing placements.

rows.verbatim: The multi-disciplinary team may be the same group that conducts the weekly review of segregation placements but shall at least include behavioral health staff, custody staff, and a federal facility supervisor.
rows.normalized: Multi-disciplinary team must at least include behavioral health staff, custody staff, and a facility supervisor.

rows.verbatim: A minimum of two Contractor employees shall be assigned each shift to verify that the segregation paperwork has been completed properly and entered in the alien's segregation file.
rows.normalized: Contractor must assign at least two employees per shift to verify segregation paperwork.

rows.verbatim: The employees shall also be responsible for gaining and maintaining access to eSRMS.
rows.normalized: Assigned Contractor employees must gain and maintain access to eSRMS.

rows.verbatim: All required documentation for the segregation population will be entered daily into eSRMS by Contractor employees.
rows.normalized: Contractor employees must enter required segregation documentation into eSRMS daily.

rows.verbatim: Note: the Contractor must comply with the needs and requirements stated in U.S. ICE Policy 11065.1: Review of the Use of Segregation for ICE Detainees.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with ICE Policy 11065.1 on Review of the Use of Segregation for ICE Detainees.

rows.verbatim:
Policies and procedures for collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information
regarding issues affecting safety, security, and the orderly running of the federal facility shall
be developed.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall develop policies and procedures for collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information affecting facility safety and security.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall include but not be limited to gang affiliations; domestic terrorist groups; tracking of aliens having advanced skills in areas of concern (locksmiths,
gunsmiths, explosives, and computers, etc.); narcotics trafficking; mail and correspondences;
alien financial information; alien telephone calls; visiting room activity; and actions of high-
profile aliens.
rows.normalized: The intelligence information the Contractor collects shall include, at minimum, gang affiliations, domestic terrorist groups, tracking of aliens with advanced skills, narcotics trafficking, mail/correspondence, alien financial information, alien telephone calls, visiting room activity, and actions of high-profile aliens (9 items).

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall share all intelligence information with the COR and ICE
officials.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall share all intelligence information with the COR and ICE officials.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall immediately report all serious incidents as outlined in the detention
standards to the field office director or designee and the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall immediately report all serious incidents to the field office director/designee and the COR.

rows.verbatim:
Serious incidents include, but are not limited to the following: activation of disturbance
control team(s); disturbances (including gang activities, group demonstrations, food boycotts, work strikes, workplace
violence, civil disturbances/protests); staff uses of force including use of lethal and less-lethal
force (includes aliens in restraints more than eight hours); assaults on staff/aliens resulting in
injuries that require medical attention (does not include routine medical evaluation after the
incident); fires; fights resulting in injuries requiring medical attention; full or partial
lockdown of the federal facility; escape; weapons discharge; suicide attempts; publicity;
adverse weather; fence damage; power outages; bomb threats; high profile alien cases
admitted to a hospital; significant environmental problems that impact the federal facility
operations; transportation accidents (e.g., airlift, bus) resulting in injuries, death or property
damage; and sexual assaults.
rows.normalized: The 'serious incidents' the Contractor must report include, but are not limited to, roughly two dozen listed incident types (disturbances, uses of force, assaults, fires, escapes, weapons discharge, suicide attempts, publicity, adverse weather, fence damage, power outages, bomb threats, hospital admissions, environmental problems, transportation accidents, sexual assaults; ~24 items total).

rows.verbatim:
Pursuant to ICE instructions, the Contractor shall counteract civil disturbances, attempts to
commit espionage or sabotage, and other acts that adversely affect the normal site conditions,
the security and safety of personnel, property, aliens, and the public.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall counteract civil disturbances, espionage/sabotage attempts, and other acts adversely affecting site security and safety, per ICE instructions.

rows.verbatim:
All
infrastructure and cabling shall be provided by the contractor in accordance with the
Attachment – CDF Design Standards – ICE – OPLA - Structured Cable Plant Standard.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide all infrastructure and cabling in accordance with the CDF Design Standards - Structured Cable Plant Standard attachment.

rows.verbatim:
NOTE: ICE IT system must be a complete, independent, and physically separate system from
the Contractor’s IT system.
rows.normalized: The ICE IT system must be a complete, independent, and physically separate system from the Contractor's IT system.

rows.verbatim:
The system shall serve all operational components including ICE
and EOIR
rows.normalized: The system shall serve all operational components, including ICE and EOIR.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor personnel shall not permit any government property to be taken away or
removed from the premises.
rows.normalized: Contractor personnel shall not permit government property to be taken away or removed from the premises.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall enact practices to safeguard and protect
government property against abuse, loss, or any other such incidents.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall enact practices to safeguard and protect government property against abuse, loss, or other incidents.

rows.verbatim:
Government property
shall be used only for official business.
rows.normalized: Government property shall be used only for official business.

rows.verbatim:
Upon expiration or
termination of this contract, the Contractor shall render a written account to the COR of all such property.
rows.normalized: Upon contract expiration/termination, Contractor must render a written account of all government property to the COR.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall assume all risks and shall be responsible for any damage to, or loss of government furnished property used by Contractor employees.
rows.normalized: Contractor must assume all risks and is responsible for damage/loss of government furnished property used by its employees.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor, upon expiration or termination of services, shall immediately transfer to the COR, all government property in its possession or in the possession of any individual or organization under its control, except as otherwise provided for in this contract.
rows.normalized: Upon expiration/termination of services, Contractor must immediately transfer all government property in its possession/control to the COR, except as otherwise provided.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall cooperate fully in transferring property to the successor Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor must cooperate fully in transferring property to a successor Contractor.

rows.verbatim: Cellular, telephone, and wireless boosters shall be provided, installed, and maintained by the Contractor to ensure optimal service throughout the federal facility and ICE and/or DOJ administrative areas.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, install, and maintain cellular/telephone/wireless boosters for optimal service facility-wide.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide well maintained and serviceable or new firearms and maintain
enough licensed firearms and ammunition to equip each armed detention officer and armed
supervisor(s) with a licensed weapon while on duty.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide well-maintained/serviceable or new firearms and maintain enough licensed firearms and ammunition to equip each armed detention officer and armed supervisor with a licensed weapon while on duty.

rows.verbatim:
Firearms may be re-issued to new
employees throughout the life of the contract if the firearm is in a serviceable condition.
rows.normalized: Contractor may re-issue firearms to new employees during the contract, provided the firearm is in serviceable condition.

rows.verbatim: Personal firearms shall not be used.
rows.normalized: Contractor personnel must not use personal firearms.

rows.verbatim:
Firearms shall be standard police service-type, semi-automatic capable of firing hollow-point
ammunition that meets the recommendations of the firearms manufacturer.
rows.normalized: Firearms provided by Contractor must be standard police service-type, semi-automatic, capable of firing hollow-point ammunition meeting the firearms manufacturer's recommendations.

rows.verbatim: Ammunition will be factory load only – no reloads.
rows.normalized: Ammunition provided must be factory load only; reloads are not permitted.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall adhere to the
manufacturer’s specifications regarding ammunition retention, e.g., ammunition shall be
properly rotated, and older ammunition utilized prior to utilization of newer ammunition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must adhere to manufacturer's specifications for ammunition retention, including rotating ammunition and using older ammunition before newer ammunition.

rows.verbatim:
All
firearms shall be licensed by the State.
rows.normalized: All firearms provided by Contractor must be licensed by the State.

rows.verbatim:
Armed officers are required to obtain a class G license
or equivalent, if required by the state.
rows.normalized: Armed officers must obtain a class G license or equivalent, if required by the state.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide enough
ammunition for each armed detention officer, including uniformed contract supervisor(s) to be
issued three full magazines.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide enough ammunition for each armed detention officer and uniformed contract supervisor to be issued three full magazines.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall account for all firearms and ammunition daily.
rows.normalized: Contractor must account for all firearms and ammunition daily.

rows.verbatim:
If any weapons or
ammunition are missing from the inventory, the COR shall be notified immediately.
rows.normalized: If any weapons or ammunition are missing from inventory, the Contractor must notify the COR immediately.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a complete listing of licensed firearms by serial numbers and by
each safe location to the COR prior to beginning performance under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a complete listing of licensed firearms by serial number and safe location to the COR before beginning contract performance.

rows.verbatim: A licensed gunsmith, in writing, shall certify all firearms safe and accurate.
rows.normalized: A licensed gunsmith must certify in writing that all firearms are safe and accurate.

rows.verbatim: Firearms shall be inspected.
rows.normalized: Firearms must be inspected.

rows.verbatim: Loading, unloading, and cleaning of the firearms shall only take place in designated areas.
rows.normalized: Loading, unloading, and cleaning of firearms must only occur in designated areas.

rows.verbatim: Firearms shall be carried with the safety on, if applicable, with a round in the chamber.
rows.normalized: Firearms must be carried with safety on (if applicable) and a round in the chamber.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall maintain appropriate and ample supplies of firearms upkeep and maintenance equipment (cleaning solvents, lubricating oil, rods, brushes, patches, and other normal maintenance tools).
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain adequate firearms upkeep/maintenance supplies.

rows.verbatim: The firearms shall be cleaned and oiled as appropriate to ensure optimum operating condition.
rows.normalized: Firearms must be cleaned and oiled as appropriate for optimum operating condition.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall obtain and maintain on file appropriate state and municipality permits and weapons permits for each officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain and keep on file state/municipality and weapons permits for each officer.

rows.verbatim: A copy of this permit shall be provided to the COR at least three working days prior to the anticipated assignment date of any individual.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a copy of the permit to the COR at least three working days before the individual's anticipated assignment date.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that its employees always have all permits and licenses in their possession while in the performance of this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure employees always carry all required permits/licenses during contract performance.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide safes/vaults for storage of firearms and ammunition, for each location where firearms are issued or exchanged, which meet ICE requirements and are approved for the storage of firearms and ammunition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide ICE-approved safes/vaults for firearm/ammunition storage at each issue/exchange location.

rows.verbatim: Contract supervisors and guards shall make accurate receipts and return entries on a Firearms and Equipment Control Register.
rows.normalized: Contract supervisors and guards must make accurate receipt/return entries on the Firearms and Equipment Control Register.

rows.verbatim: Except when issuing or returning ammunition or firearms, each safe/vault shall always remain locked.
rows.normalized: Each safe/vault must remain locked except when issuing or returning ammunition or firearms.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall change the combination of each safe/vault at least once every six months, or more often if circumstances warrant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must change each safe/vault combination at least every six months, or more often if warranted.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall certify firearms training to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor must certify firearms training to the COR.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall certify staff proficiency every quarter.
rows.normalized: Contractor must certify staff proficiency quarterly.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide an ICE approved intermediate weapon(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide ICE-approved intermediate weapon(s).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall assign one or more Contractor staff to the positions of Ammunition Control Officer and Firearms Control Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must assign one or more staff members as Ammunition Control Officer and Firearms Control Officer.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide body armor to all armed detention officers and armed supervisors.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide body armor to all armed detention officers and supervisors.

rows.verbatim: Body armor shall be worn while on armed duty.
rows.normalized: Body armor must be worn while on armed duty.

rows.verbatim: The body armor will meet all requirements set forth in the ICE Body Armor Policy.
rows.normalized: Body armor provided must meet all requirements in the ICE Body Armor Policy.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall procure replacement body armor if the body armor becomes unserviceable, ill-fitting, worn/damaged, or at the expiration of service life.
rows.normalized: Contractor must procure replacement body armor if it becomes unserviceable, ill-fitting, worn/damaged, or reaches end of service life.

rows.verbatim: When detention officers and supervisors are required to wear body armor, they shall be provided with opportunities to rehydrate and remove the body armor as necessary.
rows.normalized: When required to wear body armor, detention officers/supervisors must be given opportunities to rehydrate and remove body armor as necessary.

rows.verbatim: This shall be documented by the warden/federal facility director.
rows.normalized: The firearm inspection must be documented by the warden/federal facility director.

rows.verbatim: All armed detention officers and armed supervisors need to be made aware of the health risks associated with the wearing of body armor in high heat/high humidity conditions and/or during strenuous exertion.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make armed detention officers/supervisors aware of health risks of wearing body armor in high heat/humidity or strenuous exertion.

rows.verbatim: The use of personally owned body armor is not authorized.
rows.normalized: Personally owned body armor is not authorized for use.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide the following equipment for each officer performing services under this contract: Metal handcuffs and a handcuff carrying case. Handcuffs should be equal to or better than the basic Smith & Wesson brand. One mini-mag or comparable size, operational flashlight with batteries and a belt holder. Inclement weather apparel appropriate to local conditions. Fully operational protection equipment that meets universal protection requirements. This includes but is not limited to gloves, face masks, ear, and eye protection. Hand restraints, leg restraints and belly chains.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide specified equipment (handcuffs, flashlight, weather apparel, protective gear, restraints) for each officer performing services under the contract.

rows.verbatim: All operational protection equipment shall be replaced by the Contractor as items begin to show wear and tear.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall replace all operational protection equipment as it shows wear and tear.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will provide DHS basic records management training for all Government Contractor employees and subcontractors at the outset of their work on the contract and every year thereafter.
rows.normalized: Contractor will provide DHS records management training to all employees and subcontractors at the outset of work and annually thereafter.

rows.verbatim: A hard copy of the training will be provided as vendors will not have access to ICE systems.
rows.normalized: A hard copy of the training will be provided because vendors will not have access to ICE systems.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall maintain copies of certificates as a record of compliance.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain copies of training certificates as a compliance record.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must submit an annual e-mail notification to the Contracting Officer’s Representative that the required training has been completed for all the Contractor’s employees and subcontractors.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit an annual e-mail notification to the COR confirming required training completion for all employees and subcontractors.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall treat all federal records (as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301) under the contract as the property of the U.S. government for which the agency shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall treat all federal records under the contract as U.S. government property.

rows.verbatim: Any records containing information regarding detainees are considered Federal records and the Contractor shall comply with 8 C.F.R. §236.6.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall comply with 8 C.F.R. §236.6 regarding detainee records.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable without the expressed permission of the CO or COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable without CO/COR permission.

rows.verbatim:
The plan must include the following items:
• A statement acknowledging awareness of relevant General Records Schedules (GRS);
DHS records schedules; and ICE records schedules and their intent to comply with the
applicable retention requirements. (ICE records schedules can be found at the following
link: Records Control Schedules | National Archives)
• A summary of recordkeeping activities it plans to undertake to ensure all records are
properly maintained during the entire records lifecycle (e.g., creation, disposition, etc.).
This summary must include where and how ICE records will be stored in an acceptable
climate-controlled environment.
• A summary of electronic recordkeeping activities it plans to undertake to ensure
compliance with electronic records management (ERM) practices that are currently
underway in ICE (e.g., cloud storage, metadata management). The plan must include
details regarding any video/audio records it creates or uses and how they will be stored
during lengthy periods of time.
• A point of contact for addressing recordkeeping issues and rectifying any discrepancies
noted during a records assessment and/or inspection

Screening criteria under DHS Instruction 121-01-007, Revision 2, dated August 10, 2024,
Personnel Security, Suitability and Fitness Program, dated June 14, 2017, or successor
thereto, and Title 5, CFR part 731, dated December 18, 2024, that may exclude Contractor
employees from consideration to perform under this agreement includes:
a. Misconduct or negligence in employment.
b. Criminal conduct.
c. Material, intentional false statement or deception of fraud in examination or
appointment.
d. Dishonest conduct.
e. Excessive alcohol use, without evidence of rehabilitation, of a nature and duration that
suggests that the applicant or appointee would be prevented from performing the
duties of the position in question or would constitute a direct threat to the property or
safety of the applicant or appointee or others.
f. Illegal use of narcotics, drugs, or other controlled substances, without evidence of
substantial rehabilitation.
g. Knowing and willful engagement in acts or activities designed to overthrow the U.S.
Government by force.
h. Any statutory or regulatory bar which prevents the lawful employment of the person
involved in the position in question (for Excepted Service employees).
i. Violent conduct; and
j. Any other nondiscriminatory reason that an individual’s employment (or work on a
contract) would not protect the integrity or promote the efficiency of the service.

successor thereto, in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) automated on-line system:
• Standard Form 85P (Standard Form 85PS (with supplement to 85P required for those
with direct contact with detainees or armed positions)), “Questionnaire for Public Trust
Positions” form completed online and archived by the Contractor applicant/employee in
their NBIS eAPP account.
• Signature Release Forms (Three total) generated by NBIS eAPP upon completion of
Questionnaire (e-signature recommended/acceptable). Completed online and archived by
the Contractor applicant/employee in their NBIS eAPP account.
• Electronic fingerprints taken at an approved federal facility OR two (2) SF 87 Fingerprint
Cards (current revision) sent to OPR PSD. Additional information regarding fingerprints
will be sent to the Contractor applicant/employee from OPR PSD.
• Optional Form 306 Declaration for Federal Employment. This document is sent as an
attachment in an e-mail to the Contractor applicant/employee from OPR PSD.
• Social Security Administration 89 form (SSA-89): Authorization for the Social Security
Administration (SSA) to Release Social Security Number (SSN) Verification. This

• If occupying PREA designated position: Questionnaire regarding conduct defined under 6

an attachment in an e-mail to the Contractor applicant/employee from OPR PSD.

rows.verbatim:
d. The Contractor shall provide the means for the Government to interpret accessible
Program Data as follows:
e. Data elements and groupings of data elements shall be clearly identifiable by labels
embedded in the data itself, or by a separate schema or file layout which allows such
elements and groupings to be identified.
f. In the case of a relational database schema defined through Data Definition Language
(DDL), data elements would be represented as columns, and groupings of data would be
represented as tables. In addition, relationships between tables would be described as
foreign key relations.
g. Labels or names used to identify data elements and groupings of data elements shall be
approved by the Government. In addition, each label or name shall be associated with a
government approved definition which describes the content of data held therein.
h. Program data delivered to the Government shall conform to the Government approved
definition for each data element and grouping of data elements.
i. All data accessible by the Government shall be both machine readable and human-
readable in plain text.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide the means for the Government to interpret Program Data, including: data elements/groupings clearly identifiable by labels or schema; relational database representation via DDL; labels/names must be Government-approved and tied to Government-approved definitions; delivered data must conform to approved definitions; and data must be both machine- and human-readable; 5 sub-requirements in total.
